translations.idiomatic: Biography 54

sentences.zh: 王傑王勇宇文虯耿豪高琳李和子徹伊婁穆達奚寔劉雄侯植李延孫韋祐陳欣魏玄泉李遷哲楊乾運扶猛陽雄席固任果

translations.literal: Wang Jie, Wang Yong, Yu Wenqiu, Geng Hao, Gao Lin, Li He and his son Che, Yi Loumu, Da Xishi, Liu Xiong, Hou Zhi, Li Yansun, Wei You, Chen Xin, Wei Xuan, Quan, Li Qianzhe, Yang Ganyun, Fu Meng, Yang Xiong, Xi Gu, Ren Guo
translations.idiomatic: This chapter treats Wang Jie, Wang Yong, Yu Wenqiu, Geng Hao, Gao Lin, Li He and his son Che, Yi Loumu, Da Xishi, Liu Xiong, Hou Zhi, Li Yansun, Wei You, Chen Xin, Wei Xuan, Quan, Li Qianzhe, Yang Ganyun, Fu Meng, Yang Xiong, Xi Gu, and Ren Guo.

sentences.zh: 王傑，金城直城人也，本名文達。

translations.literal: Wang Jie was a native of Zhicheng in Jincheng commandery; his original name was Wenda.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie came from Zhicheng in Jincheng; he was originally named Wenda.

sentences.zh: 父巢，魏榆中鎮將。

translations.literal: His father Chao served as garrison commander of Yuzhong in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chao had been the Wei garrison commander at Yuzhong.

sentences.zh: 傑少有壯志，每以功名自許。

translations.literal: Jie had lofty ambitions from youth and constantly pledged himself to achieve fame and merit.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Jie burned with ambition and always measured himself by deeds of fame.

sentences.zh: 從孝武西遷，賜爵都昌縣子。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Xiaowu in the westward move and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Duchang county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved the court west, Jie was enfeoffed as Viscount of Duchang.

sentences.zh: 周文奇其才，嘗謂諸將曰：「王文達萬人敵也，但恐勇決太過耳。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou marveled at his talent and once told the generals, "Wang Wenda is a match for ten thousand men, but I fear his daring resolve may go too far.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai admired his gifts and once told the commanders, "Wang Wenda can face ten thousand foes alone—yet I worry his boldness may run away with him.

sentences.zh: 從復潼關，破沙苑，爭河橋，戰芒山，皆以勇敢聞。

translations.literal: He followed in the recovery of Tong Pass, the defeat at Shayuan, the struggle for Heqiao Bridge, and the battle at Mangshan, winning renown everywhere for courage.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in the retaking of Tong Pass, the victory at Shayuan, the contest for Heqiao Bridge, and the battle at Mangshan, and everywhere his bravery was celebrated.

sentences.zh: 親待日隆，於是賜姓宇文氏，進爵為公。

translations.literal: As personal favor toward him grew daily, he was granted the surname Yuwen and advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: His standing at court rose day by day; he was given the surname Yuwen and promoted to duke.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Palace Attendant, General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, and Director with the same ceremonial privileges as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of Palace Attendant, General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, and Director with the ceremonial standing of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 恭帝元年，從於謹圍江陵。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Gongdi reign, he followed Yu Jin in besieging Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Gongdi, he marched with Yu Jin to besiege Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 時柵內有人，善用長槊，將士登者，多為所斃。

translations.literal: At that time someone inside the palisade was skilled with the long spear; many of the men who climbed up were killed by him.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the stockade stood a man expert with the long spear; most soldiers who scaled the wall were struck down by him.

sentences.zh: 謹令傑射之，應弦而倒。

translations.literal: Jin ordered Jie to shoot him, and at the twang of the bowstring the man fell.
translations.idiomatic: Jin ordered Jie to shoot him down, and the arrow flew true—the man collapsed at once.

sentences.zh: 登者乃得入，遂拔之。

translations.literal: Only then could the climbers enter, and the place was taken.
translations.idiomatic: With him gone the assault troops broke in, and the strongpoint was captured.

sentences.zh: 謹曰：「濟我大事者在公此箭也。」

translations.literal: Jin said, "The man who will see my great undertaking through is you—and this arrow of yours.
translations.idiomatic: Jin said, "The one who will carry my great design to completion is you, and this arrow of yours.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐祚，進爵張掖郡公，為河州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, Jie was advanced to Duke of Zhangye commandery and appointed Governor of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Jie was made Duke of Zhangye and appointed Governor of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 朝延以傑勳望俱重，故授以本州。

translations.literal: The court, because Jie's merit and prestige were both weighty, therefore invested him with his home province.
translations.idiomatic: Because both his achievements and his standing were exceptional, the court gave him his native province.

sentences.zh: 後與隨公楊忠自漠北伐齊。

translations.literal: Later he joined Duke Sui Yang Zhong in a northern campaign against Qi from the desert frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Later he campaigned north against Qi from the desert marches together with Duke Sui Yang Zhong.

sentences.zh: 又從齊公憲東禦齊將斛律明月。

translations.literal: He also followed Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian east to resist the Qi general Hulu Mingyue.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian east to hold off the Qi commander Hulu Mingyue.

sentences.zh: 進位柱國。

translations.literal: He was advanced to pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 建德初，除涇州總管，頗為百姓所慕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jiande era he was appointed Grand Governor of Jingzhou and was much admired by the people.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiande reign he became Grand Governor of Jingzhou and won the people's deep regard.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，拜上柱國。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan acceded, he was appointed Senior Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, he was named Senior Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 贈七州諸軍事、河州刺史，追封鄂國公，諡曰威。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given charge of military affairs in seven provinces and the governorship of Hezhou, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of E state, with the posthumous title Wei.
translations.idiomatic: After death he was granted authority over military affairs in seven provinces and the governorship of Hezhou, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of E, and given the temple name Wei.

sentences.zh: 子孝遷，位開府儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: His son Xiaoqian held the rank of Grand Director with the ceremonial standing of a great general.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaoqian rose to Grand Director with the ceremonial rank of a great general.

sentences.zh: 王勇，代武川人也，本名胡仁。

translations.literal: Wang Yong was a native of Wuchuan in Dai; his original name was Huren.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong came from Wuchuan in Dai; he had been called Huren.

sentences.zh: 少雄健，有膽決。

translations.literal: In youth he was powerfully built and resolute in courage.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was powerfully built and fearless in action.

sentences.zh: 數從侯莫陳悅、賀拔嶽征討，功居多，拜別將。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed Hou Mo Chen Yue and Heba Yue on campaigns; his achievements were numerous, and he was appointed Vice-General.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again and again under Hou Mo Chen Yue and Heba Yue, won many honors, and was made Vice-General.

sentences.zh: 周文為丞相，封包信縣子。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Tai became Chancellor, Yong was enfeoffed as Viscount of Baoxin county.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai became Chancellor, he enfeoffed Yong as Viscount of Baoxin.

sentences.zh: 從禽竇泰，復弘農，戰沙苑，氣蓋眾軍，所當必破。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Dou Tai, the recovery of Hongnong, and the battle at Shayuan; his spirit overawed the whole army, and whatever he faced he broke.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and fighting at Shayuan; his dash outshone the entire host, and nothing in his path held.

sentences.zh: 周文歎其勇敢，賞賜特隆，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai sighed at his bravery and rewarded him with exceptional generosity, advancing him to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai marveled at his valor, heaped rewards upon him, and raised him to duke.

sentences.zh: 大軍不利，唯胡仁及王文達、耿令貴三人力戰，皆有殊功。

translations.literal: When the main army fared badly, only Huren together with Wang Wenda and Geng Linggui fought on with all their strength, each winning extraordinary merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the army met disaster, only Huren, Wang Wenda, and Geng Linggui fought on with desperate force, each earning extraordinary credit.

sentences.zh: 軍還，拜上州刺史，以雍州、岐州、北雍州擬授胡仁等。

translations.literal: After the army returned, he was appointed Governor of Shangzhou, and Yong, Huren, and the others were slated to receive Yongzhou, Qizhou, and Northern Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the army came home he was made Governor of Shangzhou; Yongzhou, Qizhou, and Northern Yongzhou were set aside for Huren and his comrades.

sentences.zh: 然州頗有優劣，文令探籌取之。

translations.literal: The provinces, however, differed in quality, and Yuwen Tai had them draw lots to decide.
translations.idiomatic: The provinces were not equal in value, so Yuwen Tai had them draw lots.

sentences.zh: 胡仁遂得雍州，文達得岐州，令貴得北雍州。

translations.literal: Huren thus received Yongzhou, Wenda received Qizhou, and Linggui received Northern Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huren drew Yongzhou, Wenda drew Qizhou, and Linggui drew Northern Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 仍賜胡仁名勇，令貴名豪，文達名傑，以彰其功。

translations.literal: Huren was then given the name Yong, Linggui the name Hao, and Wenda the name Jie, to display their merit.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Huren was granted the name Yong, Linggui the name Hao, and Wenda the name Jie, in honor of their deeds.

sentences.zh: 進侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Palace Attendant, General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, and Director with the ceremonial privileges of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant, General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, and Director with the ceremonial standing of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 恭帝元年，從柱國趙貴征蠕蠕，破之，進爵新陽郡公，賜姓庫汗氏。

translations.literal: In the first year of Gongdi he followed the pillar of state Zhao Gui against the Rouran, defeated them, was advanced to Duke of Xinyang commandery, and was granted the surname Kuhan.
translations.idiomatic: In Gongdi's first year he marched with Pillar of State Zhao Gui against the Rouran, routed them, was made Duke of Xinyang, and received the surname Kuhan.

sentences.zh: 又論討蠕蠕功，別封永固縣伯。

translations.literal: For his merit in the Rouran campaign he received a separate enfeoffment as Earl of Yonggu county.
translations.idiomatic: For the Rouran campaign he received a separate enfeoffment as Earl of Yonggu.

sentences.zh: 時有別封者，例聽回授次子，勇獨請封兄子興，時人義之。

translations.literal: At that time those with separate enfeoffments were by rule allowed to transfer them to a second son, but Yong alone asked that his elder brother's son Xing receive the fief, and men of the time praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Normally a separate fief could be reassigned to a younger son, but Yong alone asked that his brother's son Xing receive it, and contemporaries honored his fairness.

sentences.zh: 尋進位大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to great general.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Great General.

sentences.zh: 勇性雄猛，為當時驍將。

translations.literal: Yong's nature was fierce and bold, and he was the fiercest commander of his day.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was by nature ferocious and bold—the most feared fighting general of the age.

sentences.zh: 矜功伐善，好論人之惡，時論亦以此鄙之。

translations.literal: He boasted of his achievements and disparaged others' virtues, and delighted in speaking of people's faults; public opinion likewise despised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: He flaunted his own deeds, belittled others' worth, and loved to retail their faults; opinion despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 柱國侯莫陳崇勳高望重，與諸將同謁晉公護，聞勇數論人短，乃於眾中折辱之。

translations.literal: The pillar of state Hou Mo Chen Chong, whose merit and standing were high, went with the other generals to call on Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu; hearing that Yong often discussed others' shortcomings, Chong publicly humiliated him before the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar of State Hou Mo Chen Chong, a man of towering merit, visited Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu with the other commanders; when he heard Yong habitually traduced others, he shamed him before the whole company.

sentences.zh: 勇慚恚，因疽發背卒。

translations.literal: Ashamed and enraged, Yong died of a carbuncle on his back.
translations.idiomatic: Burning with shame and rage, Yong died of a carbuncle between his shoulders.

sentences.zh: 子昌嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chang succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang inherited his line.

sentences.zh: 官至大將軍。

translations.literal: He rose to the rank of great general.
translations.idiomatic: Chang rose to the rank of Great General.

sentences.zh: 宇文虯，字樂仁，代武川人也。

translations.literal: Yu Wenqiu, style name Leran, was a native of Wuchuan in Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenqiu, whose style was Leran, came from Wuchuan in Dai.

sentences.zh: 驍悍有膽略。

translations.literal: He was fierce and possessed strategic daring.
translations.idiomatic: He was ferocious in battle and bold in counsel.

sentences.zh: 少從征討，累有戰功，封南安侯。

translations.literal: From youth he followed campaigns and repeatedly won battle merit; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he campaigned repeatedly and won many honors; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 孝武西遷，以獨孤信為行台，信引虯為帳內都督。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Dugu Xin was made mobile headquarters commissioner; Xin took Qiu as commander within his personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Dugu Xin became mobile headquarters commissioner and appointed Qiu commander of his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 隨信奔梁。

translations.literal: He followed Xin in flight to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xin in flight to the Liang court.

sentences.zh: 大統三年歸闕，進爵為公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong he returned to the capital and was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong he returned to court and was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 禽竇泰，復弘農，及沙苑、河橋之戰，皆有功。

translations.literal: In the capture of Dou Tai, the recovery of Hongnong, and the battles at Shayuan and Heqiao Bridge he all had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and fighting at Shayuan and Heqiao Bridge.

sentences.zh: 又從獨孤信討梁仚定，破之。

translations.literal: He also followed Dugu Xin in attacking Liang's Xian Ding and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Dugu Xin against Liang's Xian Ding and routed him.

sentences.zh: 累遷南秦州刺史、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Governor of Southern Qinzhou, General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, and Director with the ceremonial privileges of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Governor of Southern Qinzhou, General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, and Director with the ceremonial standing of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 虯每經行陣，必身先士卒，故上下同心，戰無不克。

translations.literal: Whenever Qiu passed through the battle line he always led from the front, so officers and men were of one mind and no fight was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Qiu entered the line of battle he led from the front; officers and men fought as one, and he never knew defeat.

sentences.zh: 後除金州刺史、大將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Jinzhou and great general.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Governor of Jinzhou and Great General.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 耿豪，钜鹿人也，本名令貴。

translations.literal: Geng Hao was a native of Julu; his original name was Linggui.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Hao came from Julu; he had been called Linggui.

sentences.zh: 其先家于武川。

translations.literal: His forebears had settled in Wuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long lived in Wuchuan.

sentences.zh: 豪少粗獷，有武藝，好以氣陵人。

translations.literal: In youth Hao was rough and uncouth, skilled in martial arts, and fond of browbeating others by sheer force of spirit.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Hao was coarse and overbearing, trained in arms, and loved to intimidate others.

sentences.zh: 賀拔嶽西征，引為帳內。

translations.literal: When Heba Yue campaigned west, he took Hao into his personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: On Heba Yue's western campaign Hao entered his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 岳被害，歸周文，以武勇見知。

translations.literal: After Yue was murdered, Hao returned to Yuwen Tai and was recognized for martial valor.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue was killed, Hao joined Yuwen Tai and won notice for courage in arms.

sentences.zh: 豪亦自謂所事得主。

translations.literal: Hao also considered that he had found a worthy lord to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Hao likewise believed he had found a lord worthy of his service.

sentences.zh: 從討侯莫陳悅及迎孝武，錄前後功，封平原子。

translations.literal: He followed in the punitive campaign against Hou Mo Chen Yue and in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu; his earlier and later achievements were recorded, and he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He fought against Hou Mo Chen Yue and helped welcome Emperor Xiaowu; for his whole record of service he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之戰，豪殺傷甚多，血染甲裳盡赤。

translations.literal: In the battle at Shayuan Hao killed and wounded many; blood soaked his armor until his robes were wholly red.
translations.idiomatic: At Shayuan Hao killed and wounded in great numbers; blood drenched his armor until his battle coat ran red.

sentences.zh: 周文歎曰：「令貴武猛，所向無前，觀其甲裳，足以為驗，不須更論級數也。」

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai sighed and said, "Linggui is fierce in war and advances without peer; look at his armor and robes—that is proof enough; there is no need to count the number of heads.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai exclaimed, "Linggui fights like a tiger and cuts through every line—his blood-soaked armor tells the tale; we need not tally ranks of the slain.

sentences.zh: 進爵為公。

translations.literal: He was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 從周文戰芒山，豪謂所部曰：「大丈夫除賊，須右手拔刀，左手把槊，直斫直刺，慎莫畏死。」

translations.literal: Following Yuwen Tai at the battle of Mangshan, Hao told his troops, "When a true man destroys bandits he must draw his blade with the right hand and grip his spear with the left, hacking and thrusting straight on—take care not to fear death.
translations.idiomatic: At Mangshan Hao told his men, "A real man kills rebels with blade in his right hand and spear in his left—cut straight, thrust straight, and never flinch from death.

sentences.zh: 遂大呼獨入，敵人鋒刃亂下，當時咸謂豪歿。

translations.literal: Then he shouted and charged in alone; enemy blades rained down, and at the time all thought Hao had perished.
translations.idiomatic: He roared and plunged in alone; enemy steel fell on him from every side, and for a moment all believed him dead.

sentences.zh: 俄然奮刀而還。

translations.literal: Presently he swung his blade and came back out.
translations.idiomatic: Then he hacked his way out again.

sentences.zh: 戰數合，當豪前者死傷相繼。

translations.literal: After several clashes, those who stood before Hao fell wounded or dead in succession.
translations.idiomatic: After several rounds everyone who faced him lay dead or dying.

sentences.zh: 又謂左右曰：「吾豈樂殺人，但壯士除賊，不得不爾。

translations.literal: He also told those beside him, "Do I delight in killing men? But when a stalwart destroys bandits, he cannot do otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: He told his attendants, "Do you think I love killing? A fighting man destroying rebels cannot do otherwise.

sentences.zh: 若不能殺賊，又不為人所傷，何異逐坐人也！」

translations.literal: If you cannot kill bandits and are not wounded by others, how is that different from sitting idly among the crowd!
translations.idiomatic: If you neither kill rebels nor take a wound, what are you but dead weight in the ranks?

sentences.zh: 周文嘉之。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai applauded him.

sentences.zh: 拜北雍州刺史，賜姓和稽氏。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Northern Yongzhou and granted the surname Heji.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Governor of Northern Yongzhou and given the surname Heji.

sentences.zh: 進位侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Palace Attendant, General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, and Director with the ceremonial privileges of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant, General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, and Director with the ceremonial standing of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 豪性凶悍，言多不遜，周文惜其驍勇，每優容之。

translations.literal: Hao's nature was savage and fierce; his words were often insolent, yet Yuwen Tai valued his fighting valor and always treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was brutal and his tongue often insolent, but Yuwen Tai prized his valor and always indulged him.

sentences.zh: 豪亦自謂意氣冠群，終無所屈。

translations.literal: Hao also believed his spirit outshone the whole company and that he would never yield to anyone.
translations.idiomatic: Hao likewise thought his mettle unmatched and that he would bow to no one.

sentences.zh: 李穆、蔡祐初與豪同時開府，後並居豪之右。

translations.literal: Li Mu and Cai You had at first opened their own directorates together with Hao, but later both ranked above him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu and Cai You had received directorates at the same time as Hao, yet both later outranked him.

sentences.zh: 豪不能平，謂周文曰：「人間物議，謂豪勝李穆、蔡祐。」

translations.literal: Hao could not accept this and said to Yuwen Tai, "Public talk holds that Hao surpasses Li Mu and Cai You.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to stomach it, Hao told Yuwen Tai, "People say I outdo Li Mu and Cai You.

sentences.zh: 周文曰：「何以言之？」

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai said, "On what grounds do they say so?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai asked, "What grounds do they give?"

sentences.zh: 豪曰：「人言李穆、蔡祐是丞相髆髀，耿豪、王勇，丞相咽項，以在上，故為勝也。」

translations.literal: Hao said, "People say Li Mu and Cai You are the Chancellor's thighs and shanks, while Geng Hao and Wang Yong are the Chancellor's throat and nape—because we stand above, we are held the better."
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "They call Li Mu and Cai You the Chancellor's thighs and calves, but Geng Hao and Wang Yong his throat and nape—and because we sit higher, they say we win."

sentences.zh: 豪之粗猛皆此類。

translations.literal: Hao's roughness and fierceness were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's blunt ferocity was always of this kind.

sentences.zh: 卒，周文痛惜之。

translations.literal: He died, and Yuwen Tai grieved deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When he died Yuwen Tai mourned him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 子雄嗣，位至大將軍。

translations.literal: His son Xiong succeeded him and rose to the rank of great general.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiong inherited the line and rose to Great General.

sentences.zh: 高琳，字季瑉，其先高麗人也。

translations.literal: Gao Lin, style name Jimin, was of Koguryŏ descent by ancestry.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lin, whose style was Jimin, traced his ancestry to Koguryŏ.

sentences.zh: 仕于燕，又歸魏，賜姓羽真氏。

translations.literal: He served Yan, then submitted to Wei and was granted the surname Yuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Yan state, then came over to Wei and received the surname Yuzhen.

sentences.zh: 琳母嘗祓禊泗濱，遇見一石，光彩朗潤，遂持以歸。

translations.literal: Lin's mother once performed the river purification rite on the Si bank; she came upon a stone bright and lustrous and took it home.
translations.idiomatic: His mother once bathed in the Si during the purification festival, found a stone luminous and smooth, and carried it home.

sentences.zh: 是夜，夢人衣冠有若仙者，謂曰：「夫人向所將來石，是浮磬之精。

translations.literal: That night a man in caps and robes like an immortal appeared in a dream and said, "Madam, the stone you brought back is the essence of the floating chime-stone.
translations.idiomatic: That night she dreamed of a figure in immortal garb who said, "The stone you took is the spirit of the floating sonorous stone.

sentences.zh: 若能寶持，必生令子。」

translations.literal: If you treasure and keep it, you will surely bear an outstanding son.
translations.idiomatic: Treasure it, and you will bear a fine son.

sentences.zh: 母驚寤，舉身流汗。

translations.literal: The mother awoke in alarm, and sweat broke out over her whole body.
translations.idiomatic: She woke in terror, drenched in sweat.

sentences.zh: 俄而有娠，及生，因名琳，字季瑉。

translations.literal: Before long she conceived, and when the child was born she named him Lin and gave him the style Jimin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon she was with child; at the birth she named him Lin and styled him Jimin.

sentences.zh: 從孝武西遷，封钜野縣子。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Xiaowu in the westward move and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Juye county.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xiaowu west and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Juye.

sentences.zh: 河橋之役，琳勇冠諸軍。

translations.literal: In the Heqiao campaign Lin's bravery led the whole army.
translations.idiomatic: At Heqiao Bridge his courage outshone every unit.

sentences.zh: 周文謂曰：「公即我之韓、白也。」

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai said to him, "Sir, you are my Han Xin and Bai Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai told him, "You are my Han Xin and Bai Qi.

sentences.zh: 復從戰芒山，除正平郡守。

translations.literal: He again followed in the battle at Mangshan and was appointed Administrator of Zhengping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again at Mangshan and was appointed Administrator of Zhengping.

sentences.zh: 齊將東方老來寇，琳擊之。

translations.literal: The Qi general Dongfang Lao came to raid, and Lin struck him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi commander Dongfang Lao raided the border, Lin attacked him.

sentences.zh: 老中數創乃退，謂其左右曰：「吾經陣多矣，未見如此健兒。」

translations.literal: Lao was wounded several times and then withdrew; he told those beside him, "I have been through many battle lines, but never seen such a stalwart.
translations.idiomatic: Dongfang Lao took several wounds and pulled back; he told his attendants, "I have seen many fields, but never a fighter like this.

sentences.zh: 後除鄜州刺史，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、侍中。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Fuzhou and additionally made General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, Director with the ceremonial privileges of the Three Excellencies, and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Governor of Fuzhou and promoted to General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, Director with the ceremonial standing of the Three Excellencies, and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐祚，進爵犍為郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, Lin was advanced to Duke of Qianwei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Lin was raised to Duke of Qianwei.

sentences.zh: 武成二年，討平文州氏。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wucheng he campaigned and pacified the Di of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wucheng he subdued the Di tribes of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 師還，帝宴群公卿士，仍賦詩言志。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the Emperor feasted the dukes, ministers, and scholars and also composed poetry to express his intent.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return the Emperor banqueted the nobles and officials and himself composed verse to declare his mind.

sentences.zh: 琳詩末章云：「寄言竇車騎，為謝霍將軍。

translations.literal: The closing lines of Lin's poem read, "Send word to General Dou of the chariots and cavalry, and convey my thanks to General Huo.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's poem closed with the lines, "Tell the chariot-and-cavalry general Dou, and thank for me General Huo.

sentences.zh: 何以報天子？

translations.literal: How shall we repay the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: How shall we repay the Son of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 沙漠靜妖氛。」

translations.literal: The desert lies quiet of baleful vapors.
translations.idiomatic: The desert's evil mists are stilled.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅曰：「獯、獫陸梁，未時款塞，卿言有驗，國之福也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and said, "The Xianyun and Xianyun have rampaged unrestrained and have not yet tendered allegiance at the border; your words are verified—this is the state's good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rejoiced and said, "The northern tribes have long raided without submitting; your words have come true—a blessing for the realm."

sentences.zh: 天和三年，為江陵副總管。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe he became Deputy Grand Governor of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianhe he was appointed Deputy Grand Governor of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 時陳將吳明徹來寇，總管田弘與梁主蕭巋出保紀南城，唯琳與梁僕射王操固守江陵三城以抗之。

translations.literal: At that time the Chen general Wu Mingche came to invade; Grand Governor Tian Hong together with the Liang ruler Xiao Kui went out to hold Jicheng south of the city, while only Lin together with Liang's Vice Director Wang Cao firmly defended the three cities of Jiangling to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen's Wu Mingche invaded, Tian Hong and Liang's Xiao Kui withdrew to guard Jicheng south of the city, while Lin and Liang Vice Director Wang Cao alone held Jiangling's three walled districts against him.

sentences.zh: 晝夜拒戰，凡經十旬，明徹退走。

translations.literal: Day and night they fought off the assault; in all it lasted a hundred days, and Mingche withdrew and fled.
translations.idiomatic: They resisted day and night for a hundred days until Mingche broke off and fled.

sentences.zh: 巋表言其狀，帝乃優詔追琳入朝，親加勞問。

translations.literal: Kui memorialized reporting the situation, and the Emperor thereupon issued a gracious edict recalling Lin to court and personally offered him words of consolation.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui reported the feat in a memorial, and the Emperor issued a gracious summons, receiving Lin in person with warm praise.

sentences.zh: 六年，進位柱國。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was advanced to pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 贈本官。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted his former offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted his former offices.

sentences.zh: 加五州諸軍事、冀州刺史，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: Additionally he was given charge of military affairs in five provinces and the governorship of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted authority over military affairs in five provinces and the governorship of Jizhou, with the posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子儒襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Ru succeeded to the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ru inherited the fief.

sentences.zh: 位儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: He held the rank of Grand Director with the ceremonial standing of a great general.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Director with the ceremonial rank of a great general.

sentences.zh: 李和，本名慶和，朔方岩綠人也。

translations.literal: Li He, original name Qinghe, was a native of Yanlu in Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: Li He, originally Qinghe, came from Yanlu in Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 父僧養，以累世雄豪，為夏州酋。

translations.literal: His father Sengyang, because the family had been powerful for generations, was chieftain of Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sengyang, a man of hereditary power, was chieftain of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 和少敢勇有識度，狀貌魁偉，為州裏所推。

translations.literal: In youth He was daring and courageous with judgment, of imposing stature, and was esteemed by the district.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth He was bold, far-sighted, and imposing in build, and the district looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 賀拔嶽作鎮關中，引為帳內都督。

translations.literal: When Heba Yue held the frontier command in Guanzhong, he took He into his personal guard as commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Yue governed Guanzhong, he brought He into his personal guard as commander.

sentences.zh: 後從周文，累遷侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、夏州刺史，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: Later he followed Yuwen Tai and was promoted repeatedly to Palace Attendant, General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, Director with the ceremonial privileges of the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Xiazhou, and was granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Yuwen Tai, rising to Palace Attendant, General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, Director with the ceremonial standing of the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Xiazhou, and received the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 周文嘗謂諸將曰：「宇文慶和累經任委，每稱吾意。」

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai once told the generals, "Yuwen Qinghe has repeatedly been entrusted with duties and always accords with my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai once told his commanders, "Yuwen Qinghe has served me again and again and never failed my expectations.

sentences.zh: 又賜名意焉。

translations.literal: He was also granted the name Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was also given the name Yi.

sentences.zh: 改封永豐縣公。

translations.literal: His fief was changed to Duke of Yongfeng county.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was changed to Duke of Yongfeng.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，除司憲中大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding he was appointed Grand Master of the Department of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoding he became Grand Master of the Department of Justice.

sentences.zh: 尋改封德廣郡公，出為洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon his fief was changed to Duke of Deguang commandery, and he went out as Governor of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Duke of Deguang and sent out as Governor of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 和前在夏州，頗留遺惠，及有此授，商、洛父老莫不想望德音。

translations.literal: When He had earlier been in Xiazhou he had left behind much kindness, and with this new appointment the elders of Shang and Luo all longed to hear his virtuous renown.
translations.idiomatic: He had left a legacy of kindness in Xiazhou, and when this appointment came the elders of Shang and Luo yearned for his return.

sentences.zh: 和至州，以仁恕訓物，獄訟為之簡靜。

translations.literal: When He reached the province he governed the people with benevolence and forbearance, and lawsuits became few and tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: At Luozhou he ruled with mercy and restraint, and the courts grew quiet.

sentences.zh: 進柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to pillar of state and great general.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Pillar of State and Great General.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇元年，遷上柱國。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang of Sui he was transferred to Senior Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Sui's Kaihuang reign he became Senior Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 和立身剛簡，老而逾勵，諸子趨事，若奉嚴君。

translations.literal: He conducted himself with stern integrity; in old age he grew only more rigorous, and his sons attended to affairs as if serving a strict father.
translations.idiomatic: He lived with austere integrity and grew stricter with age; his sons served him as they would a stern father.

sentences.zh: 以意是周文帝賜名，帝朝已革；

translations.literal: Because Yi was a name granted by Emperor Wen of Zhou and that dynasty had already fallen;
translations.idiomatic: The name Yi had been a gift from Emperor Wen of Zhou, and that house was gone;

sentences.zh: 慶和則父之所命，義不可違。

translations.literal: Qinghe was what his father had ordained, and by righteousness it could not be set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghe was his father's gift and could not be cast off.

sentences.zh: 至是，遂以和為名。

translations.literal: At this point he therefore took He as his name.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore took He as his name.

sentences.zh: 二年，薨。

translations.literal: In the second year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he died.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，加司徒公，諡曰肅。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted his former offices and additionally made Duke of the Department of State, with the posthumous title Su.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he kept his offices and was made Duke of the Department of State, with the posthumous name Su.

sentences.zh: 子徹嗣。

translations.literal: His son Che succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Che inherited his line.

sentences.zh: 徹字廣達。

translations.literal: Che's style name was Guangda.
translations.idiomatic: Che, whose style was Guangda,

sentences.zh: 性剛毅，有器幹。

translations.literal: His nature was firm and resolute, and he possessed capacity and administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: was firm of character and gifted with real capacity.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，從皇太子西征吐谷渾，以功賜爵周昌縣男。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou he followed the crown prince on the western campaign against Tuyuhun and for merit was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhouchang county.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he followed the crown prince west against Tuyuhun and was enfeoffed Baron of Zhouchang for his merit.

sentences.zh: 從武帝平齊，錄前後功，再進爵。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Wu in the pacification of Qi, and his earlier and later achievements were recorded; he was advanced in rank twice.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Emperor Wu to pacify Qi; his whole record of service won him two promotions in rank.

sentences.zh: 遷左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Left Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of the Left Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 及隋晉王廣鎮并州，妙選府官，詔徹總晉王府軍事，進爵齊安郡公。

translations.literal: When Prince Jin of Sui Guang held Bingzhou as his domain, outstanding officials were chosen for his staff; an edict ordered Che to oversee all military affairs of the Prince of Jin's establishment, and he was advanced to Duke of Qi'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui's Prince of Jin held Bingzhou, the court chose the finest for his staff; Che was ordered to command the prince's military affairs and was made Duke of Qi'an.

sentences.zh: 時蜀王秀亦鎮益州，上謂侍臣曰：「安得文同王子相，武如李廣達者乎！」

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Shu Xiu also held Yizhou as his domain; the Emperor told his attendants, "Where can I find a civil officer like Wang Zixiang and a martial officer like Li Guangda!
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Shu Xiu held Yizhou, the Emperor told his court, "If only I had a civil man like Wang Zixiang and a warrior like Li Guangda!

sentences.zh: 其見重如此。

translations.literal: Thus highly was he regarded.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 明年，突厥沙缽略可汗犯塞，上令衛王爽為元帥擊之，以徹為長史。

translations.literal: The next year the Türk qaghan Shabolu invaded the border; the Emperor ordered Prince Wei Shuang as commander to strike him, with Che as chief of staff.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Türk qaghan Shabolu raided the frontier; Prince Wei Shuang was made commander with Che as chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 遇虜于白道，行軍總管李充請襲之。

translations.literal: They encountered the enemy at Baidao; the campaign commander Li Chong asked to make a surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: At Baidao they met the enemy; campaign commander Li Chong proposed a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 諸將多以為疑，唯徹獎成其事，請同行，遂掩擊大破之。

translations.literal: Most of the generals were doubtful, but only Che encouraged the plan and asked to go along; they made a concealed strike and routed the enemy utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Most commanders hesitated, but Che alone urged the plan and volunteered to go; the ambush shattered the Türk host.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略棄所服金甲而遁。

translations.literal: Shabolu abandoned the golden armor he wore and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shabolu cast off his golden armor and fled.

sentences.zh: 以功加上大將軍。

translations.literal: For merit he was made Senior Great General.
translations.idiomatic: For this feat he was made Senior Great General.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略因此稱籓。

translations.literal: Shabolu therefore declared himself a vassal.
translations.idiomatic: Shabolu thereupon submitted as a vassal.

sentences.zh: 改封安道郡公。

translations.literal: His fief was changed to Duke of Andao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was changed to Duke of Andao.

sentences.zh: 開皇十年，進位柱國。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaihuang he was advanced to pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Kaihuang he was promoted to Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 及晉王為揚州總管，以徹為司馬，改封德廣郡公。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin became Grand Governor of Yangzhou, Che was made his Chief Administrator and his fief was changed to Duke of Deguang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin became Grand Governor of Yangzhou, Che became his Chief Administrator and was made Duke of Deguang.

sentences.zh: 尋徙封城陽郡公。

translations.literal: Soon his fief was transferred to Duke of Chengyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his fief was moved to Chengyang.

sentences.zh: 其後突厥犯塞，徹復領行軍總管破之。

translations.literal: Afterward when the Türks again invaded the border, Che once more led the campaign command and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Türks raided again, Che once more led the field army and broke them.

sentences.zh: 及左僕射高熲得罪，以徹素與熲善，被疏忌。

translations.literal: When Left Vice Director Gao Bin fell from favor, because Che had long been on good terms with Bin he came under suspicion and estrangement.
translations.idiomatic: When Left Vice Director Gao Bin was disgraced, Che's old friendship with him brought suspicion and coldness from the throne.

sentences.zh: 後出怨言，上聞，召入臥內賜宴，言及平生，因遇鳩卒。

translations.literal: Later he uttered complaints; when the Emperor heard of it he summoned him into the inner chamber for a banquet and spoke of their whole lives together, and on that occasion he met death by poisoned wine.
translations.idiomatic: Later he grumbled; the Emperor heard, summoned him to a private banquet, spoke of old times—and had him poisoned.

sentences.zh: 大業中，其妻元氏為孽子安遠誣以咒詛，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the Daye era his wife the Lady Yuan was by the illegitimate son Anyuan falsely accused of cursing the throne and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye era his wife Lady Yuan was framed for sorcery by the bastard son Anyuan and put to death.

sentences.zh: 伊婁穆，字奴幹，代人也。

translations.literal: Yi Loumu, style name Nugan, was a native of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Loumu, whose style was Nugan, came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 父靈，善騎射，為周文所知，嘗謂之曰：「若伊尹阿衡于殷，致主堯、舜。

translations.literal: His father Ling was skilled in mounted archery and was known to Yuwen Tai, who once told him, "If Yi Yin assisted Yin and balanced the state, bringing the ruler to the level of Yao and Shun—
translations.idiomatic: His father Ling excelled at mounted archery and won Yuwen Tai's notice; Tai once told him, "Yi Yin aided Yin and raised his lord to the level of Yao and Shun—

sentences.zh: 卿既姓伊，庶卿不替前緒。」

translations.literal: Since your surname is Yi, I hope you will not fall short of that earlier record.
translations.idiomatic: You bear the surname Yi; may you not fall short of that precedent.

sentences.zh: 於是賜名尹焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was granted the name Yin.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore given the name Yin.

sentences.zh: 曆衛將軍、隆州刺史、盧奴縣公。

translations.literal: He served as General of the Guard, Governor of Longzhou, and Duke of Lunü county.
translations.idiomatic: He served as General of the Guard, Governor of Longzhou, and Duke of Lunü.

sentences.zh: 穆弱冠為周文帳內親信，以機辯見知。

translations.literal: In his weak-crown years Mu became a trusted intimate in Yuwen Tai's personal guard and was recognized for quick wit and eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Mu entered Yuwen Tai's personal guard and won notice for quick wit.

sentences.zh: 曆中書舍人、通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He served as Attendant of the Secretariat and Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Attendant of the Secretariat and Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 嘗入白事，周文望見悅之，字之曰：「奴幹作儀同面見我矣。」

translations.literal: Once when he came in to report business, Yuwen Tai saw him from afar and was pleased; he addressed him by his style and said, "Nugan has come to see me with the face of a Director of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Once, reporting to court, he pleased Yuwen Tai at a distance; Tai said by his style, "Nugan comes before me with the bearing of a Director of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 於是拜儀同三司，賜封安陽縣伯。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed Director of the Third Rank and enfeoffed as Earl of Anyang county.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon made Director of the Third Rank and enfeoffed Earl of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，進位驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, he was advanced to General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was promoted to General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 建德中，卒。

translations.literal: In the Jiande era he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiande era he died.

sentences.zh: 達奚寔，字什伏代，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Da Xishi, style name Shifudai, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Da Xishi, whose style was Shifudai, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父顯相，武衛將軍。

translations.literal: His father Xianxiang was a General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xianxiang had been a General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 寔少修立，有幹局。

translations.literal: In youth Shi was upright in conduct and possessed administrative capacity.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was upright and capable in administration.

sentences.zh: 從魏孝武西遷，封臨汾縣伯。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei in the westward move and was enfeoffed as Earl of Linfen county.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xiaowu west and was enfeoffed Earl of Linfen.

sentences.zh: 從周文禽竇泰，復弘農，破沙苑，皆力戰有功。

translations.literal: He followed Yuwen Tai in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and breaking Shayuan, fighting with all his strength and winning merit in each.
translations.idiomatic: He fought with Yuwen Tai at the capture of Dou Tai, the recovery of Hongnong, and the victory at Shayuan.

sentences.zh: 累遷相府從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Attendant of the Chancellor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Attendant of the Chancellor's Office.

sentences.zh: 寔性嚴重，深見器遇。

translations.literal: Shi's nature was stern and grave, and he was deeply trusted and favored.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and grave by nature, he won deep trust.

sentences.zh: 六官建，行蕃部中大夫，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵平陽縣公。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established he served as Grand Master of the Barbarian Affairs Bureau, was additionally made General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry and Director with the ceremonial privileges of the Three Excellencies, and was advanced to Duke of Pingyang county.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were set up he became Grand Master of the Barbarian Affairs Bureau, was made General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry and Director with the ceremonial standing of the Three Excellencies, and was raised to Duke of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 周保定初，卒于刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou's Baoding era he died while serving as governor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Baoding he died in office as governor.

sentences.zh: 諡曰恭。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He received the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 子豐嗣。

translations.literal: His son Feng succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Feng inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 劉雄，字猛雀，臨洮子城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiong, style name Mengque, was a native of Zicheng in Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiong, whose style was Mengque, came from Zicheng in Lintao.

sentences.zh: 少機辯，慷慨有大志，初為周文親信，後拜中大夫，兼中書舍人，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: In youth he was quick and eloquent, generous and possessed of great ambition; at first he was a trusted intimate of Yuwen Tai, later was appointed Grand Master and concurrently Attendant of the Secretariat, and was granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and ambitious, he first served Yuwen Tai as a trusted intimate, later became Grand Master and concurrent Attendant of the Secretariat, and received the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，加大都督。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, he was made Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was made Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 天和中，累遷驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，封周昌侯。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era he was promoted repeatedly to General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry and Director with the ceremonial privileges of the Three Excellencies, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhouchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianhe era he rose to General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry and Director with the ceremonial standing of the Three Excellencies and was enfeoffed Marquis of Zhouchang.

sentences.zh: 歷位納言、內史中大夫、候正。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Chief Counselor, Grand Master of the Inner Scribes, and Director of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Chief Counselor, Grand Master of the Inner Scribes, and Director of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗從容謂曰：「古人云：'富貴不歸故鄉，猶衣錦夜遊。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once said to him at leisure, "The ancients said: 'Wealth and honor that do not return to one's homeland are like brocade worn on a night walk.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once said to him gently, "The ancients said, 'Wealth and honor that never return home are like brocade worn only at night.

sentences.zh: '」乃以雄為河州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xiong was appointed Governor of Hezhou.'
translations.idiomatic: He then made Xiong Governor of Hezhou.'

sentences.zh: 雄先已為本縣令，復有此授，鄉里榮之。

translations.literal: Xiong had already been magistrate of his home county; with this further appointment his home district was honored.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong had already been magistrate of his home county; this new post brought glory to his homeland.

sentences.zh: 及皇太子西征吐谷渾，雄自涼州從滕王道先入，功居多，加上開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When the crown prince campaigned west against Tuyuhun, Xiong from Liangzhou followed the Prince of Teng's route in the vanguard; his achievements were numerous, and he was additionally made Senior Director with the ceremonial privileges of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: On the crown prince's western campaign against Tuyuhun, Xiong marched from Liangzhou with Prince Teng's vanguard and won great credit; he was made Senior Director with the ceremonial standing of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 從平并州，拜上大將軍，進爵趙郡公。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of Bingzhou and was appointed Senior Great General and advanced to Duke of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify Bingzhou, was made Senior Great General, and was raised to Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 平鄴城，進柱國。

translations.literal: When Yecheng was pacified he was advanced to pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: When Yecheng fell he was promoted to Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年，突厥寇幽州，雄戰歿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng the Türks raided Youzhou and Xiong died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuanzheng the Türks raided Youzhou and Xiong fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 贈亳州總管。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted the post of Grand Governor of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Grand Governor of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 子升嗣。

translations.literal: His son Sheng succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sheng inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 以雄死王事，授儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: Because Xiong died in service to the state, Sheng was granted the rank of Grand Director with the ceremonial standing of a great general.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xiong died in the state's service, Sheng was granted the ceremonial rank of Grand Director and great general.

sentences.zh: 侯植，字仁幹，其先上穀人也。

translations.literal: Hou Zhi, style name Rengan, was of Shanggu descent by ancestry.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhi, whose style was Rengan, traced his ancestry to Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 高祖恕，為北地太守，子孫因家於北地之三水。

translations.literal: His ancestor Shu was Governor of Beidi, and the family thereafter settled at Sanshui in Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: An ancestor named Shu had been Governor of Beidi, and the clan then made its home at Sanshui in Beidi.

sentences.zh: 植少倜儻，有大節，容貌奇偉，武藝絕倫。

translations.literal: In youth Zhi was free-spirited and possessed great integrity; his appearance was extraordinarily imposing and his martial skill unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was bold and high-minded, of striking presence and unmatched in arms.

sentences.zh: 仕魏為義州刺史，甚有政績。

translations.literal: He served Wei as Governor of Yizhou and achieved notable administrative success.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei service he governed Yizhou with a strong record of good rule.

sentences.zh: 後從孝武西遷，賜姓侯伏侯氏。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Xiaowu in the westward move and was granted the surname Houfuhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Emperor Xiaowu west and received the surname Houfuhou.

sentences.zh: 從周文破沙苑，戰河橋，進大都督。

translations.literal: He followed Yuwen Tai in breaking Shayuan and fighting at Heqiao Bridge and was advanced to Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He fought with Yuwen Tai at Shayuan and Heqiao Bridge and was made Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 涼州刺史宇文仲和據州作逆，植從開府獨孤信討禽之，封肥城縣公，賜姓賀屯氏。

translations.literal: Yuwen Zhonghe, Governor of Liangzhou, held the province in rebellion; Zhi followed the directorate commander Dugu Xin to capture him, was enfeoffed as Duke of Feicheng county, and was granted the surname Hetun.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Zhonghe rebelled in Liangzhou, Zhi followed Dugu Xin to take him, was enfeoffed Duke of Feicheng, and received the surname Hetun.

sentences.zh: 後從于謹平江陵，進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，別封一子氵開源縣伯。

translations.literal: Later he followed Yu Jin in pacifying Jiangling, was advanced to General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry and Director with the ceremonial privileges of the Three Excellencies, and one son was separately enfeoffed as Earl of Kaiyuan county.
translations.idiomatic: He later helped Yu Jin pacify Jiangling, rose to General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry and Director with the ceremonial standing of the Three Excellencies, and one son received a separate fief as Earl of Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 周孝文帝踐阼，進爵郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen of Zhou ascended the throne, Zhi was advanced to Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen of Zhou took the throne, he was raised to commandery duke.

sentences.zh: 時帝幼沖，晉公護執政，植從兄龍恩為護所親。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor was young and Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu held power; Zhi's cousin Long'en was favored by Hu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still a child and Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu ruled; Zhi's cousin Long'en enjoyed Hu's favor.

sentences.zh: 及護誅趙貴，諸宿將等多不自安。

translations.literal: When Hu executed Zhao Gui, many of the veteran generals were ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu killed Zhao Gui, the senior commanders grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 植謂從兄龍恩曰：「主上春秋既富。

translations.literal: Zhi told his cousin Long'en, "Our lord is already grown in years.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi told Long'en, "The emperor is no longer young.

sentences.zh: 安危系於數公，若多誅戮，自立威權，何止社稷有累卵之危，恐吾宗亦緣此敗。

translations.literal: The state's safety rests on a few men; if they slaughter many to build their own authority, not only will the altars face danger like an egg in a pile, but I fear our clan will be ruined as well.
translations.idiomatic: If they kill widely to build private power, the realm will totter like a piled egg—and our house may fall with it.

sentences.zh: 兄安得知而不言！」

translations.literal: Brother, how can you know this and not speak!
translations.idiomatic: Brother, how can you know this and stay silent?

sentences.zh: 龍恩竟不能用。

translations.literal: Long'en in the end could not adopt the counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Long'en would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 植又承間言於護曰：「公以骨肉之親，當社稷之寄，願推誠王室，擬跡伊、周，則率土幸甚。」

translations.literal: Zhi also seized an opportunity to tell Hu, "As a bone-and-flesh kinsman bearing the state's charge, I pray you will show sincere loyalty to the imperial house and take Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou as your model—then all within the seas will be fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi also urged Hu privately, "You are kin to the throne and hold the realm in trust; model yourself on Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, and the empire will rejoice.

sentences.zh: 護曰：「我誓以身報國，卿豈謂吾有他志邪？」

translations.literal: Hu said, "I swear to repay the state with my body—do you suppose I harbor other designs?"
translations.idiomatic: Hu replied, "I have sworn to give my life for the state—do you think me disloyal?"

sentences.zh: 又聞其先與龍恩言，乃陰忌之。

translations.literal: When he also heard of Zhi's earlier talk with Long'en, he came to regard Zhi with secret resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of the talk with Long'en, Hu began to resent him.

sentences.zh: 植懼不免禍，遂以憂卒。

translations.literal: Zhi, fearing he could not escape disaster, died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he could not escape ruin, Zhi died of grief.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍、平州刺史，諡曰節。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted the rank of great general and Governor of Pingzhou, with the posthumous title Jie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Great General and Governor of Pingzhou, with the posthumous name Jie.

sentences.zh: 子定嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ding succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ding inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 及護伏誅，龍恩及其弟萬壽並預其禍。

translations.literal: When Hu was executed, Long'en and his brother Wanshou both perished in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu was put to death, Long'en and his brother Wanshou died in the purge.

sentences.zh: 武帝以植忠於朝廷，特免其子孫。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, because Zhi had been loyal to the court, specially exempted his sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu spared Zhi's descendants because of his loyalty to the throne.

sentences.zh: 李延孫，伊川人也。

translations.literal: Li Yansun was a native of Yichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yansun came from Yichuan.

sentences.zh: 父長壽，性雄豪，少與蠻酋結托，侵掠闕南。

translations.literal: His father Changshou was by nature bold and heroic; in youth he allied with barbarian chiefs and raided south of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: His father Changshou was fierce and in youth joined barbarian leaders in raiding south of the passes.

sentences.zh: 魏孝昌中，朝議恐其為亂，乃以長壽為防蠻都督，給其鼓節。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era of Wei Xiaoming, the court feared he would stir rebellion and therefore appointed Changshou Commander for Barbarian Defense, giving him drums and banners of office.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei Xiaoming's Xiaochang era the court, fearing revolt, made Changshou Commander for Barbarian Defense with full insignia of command.

sentences.zh: 長壽盡其智力，防遏群蠻，伊川左右，寇盜為之稍息。

translations.literal: Changshou exerted all his wit and strength, held the various barbarians in check, and on both banks of the Yichuan banditry gradually quieted.
translations.idiomatic: Changshou used every resource to restrain the tribes, and banditry along the Yichuan eased.

sentences.zh: 永安之後，長壽徒侶日盛，魏帝藉其力用，因而撫之。

translations.literal: After the Yong'an era Changshou's following grew daily; the Wei Emperor relied on his strength and therefore conciliated him.
translations.idiomatic: After Yong'an his following swelled; the Wei emperor leaned on his power and treated him with favor.

sentences.zh: 累遷北華州刺史，賜爵清河郡公。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Governor of Northern Huazhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Governor of Northern Huazhou and was enfeoffed Duke of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 及孝武西遷，長壽率勵義士拒東魏。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Changshou led righteous men to resist Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Changshou rallied loyalists against Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 後為廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he became Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 東魏遣行台侯景攻之，城陷，遇害。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei sent mobile headquarters commander Hou Jing to attack him; the city fell and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei sent Hou Jing against him; the city fell and he was slain.

sentences.zh: 追贈太尉。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 延孫亦雄武，有將率才略，少從長壽征討，以勇敢聞。

translations.literal: Yansun was also martial and possessed talent for command and strategy; in youth he followed Changshou on campaigns and was known for bravery.
translations.idiomatic: Yansun was warlike and strategic; he campaigned with his father from youth and won fame for courage.

sentences.zh: 賀拔勝為荊州刺史，表延孫為都督，肅清鵶路，頗有力焉。

translations.literal: When Heba Sheng was Governor of Jingzhou he memorialized Yansun as commander; he cleared the Yalu road and contributed solid strength.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Sheng, as Governor of Jingzhou, recommended him as commander; he secured the Yalu route and did real service.

sentences.zh: 及長壽被害，延孫乃還，收集其父之眾。

translations.literal: When Changshou was killed, Yansun returned and gathered his father's troops.
translations.idiomatic: After Changshou's death Yansun came back and rallied his father's men.

sentences.zh: 自孝武西遷後，朝士流亡。

translations.literal: After Emperor Xiaowu moved west, courtiers fled in exile.
translations.idiomatic: After the western move, officials fled in streams.

sentences.zh: 廣陵王欣、錄尚書長孫承業、穎川王斌之、安昌王子均及建甯、江夏、隴東諸王並百官等攜持妻子來投延孫者，即率眾衛送，並贈以珍玩，咸達關中。

translations.literal: Prince of Guangling Xin, Chief Secretary of the Records Sun Chengye, Prince of Yingchuan Binzhi, Prince of Anchang Zijun, and the princes of Jianning, Jiangxia, and Longdong together with officials of every rank came to join Yansun carrying wives and children; he led troops to escort and protect them and gave them treasures, and all reached Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and high officials—Xin of Guangling, Sun Chengye, Binzhi of Yingchuan, Zijun of Anchang, and many more—fled to him with families; he escorted them with his troops, gave gifts, and saw them safe to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 齊神武深患之，遣行台慕容紹宗等數道攻擊，延孫大破之。

translations.literal: Qi Emperor Shenwu deeply dreaded him and sent mobile headquarters Murong Shaozong and others along several routes to attack; Yansun defeated them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's Shenwu dreaded him and sent Murong Shaozong against him on several routes; Yansun crushed them.

sentences.zh: 乃授延孫京南行台、節度河南諸軍事、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Mobile Headquarters of the Capital South, commander of military affairs in Henan, and Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Mobile Headquarters of the Capital South, commander of Henan military affairs, and Governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋進車騎大將軍、儀同三司、大都督，賜爵華山郡公。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Director of the Third Rank, and Grand Commander, and enfeoffed as Duke of Huashan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became General of Chariots and Cavalry, Director of the Third Rank, Grand Commander, and Duke of Huashan.

sentences.zh: 延孫既蒙重委，每以克清伊、洛為已任，頻以寡擊眾，威振敵境。

translations.literal: Having received this weighty trust, Yansun always took clearing Yi and Luo as his own charge; repeatedly with few he struck many and his prestige shook the enemy frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted with the eastern front, he made clearing the Yi and Luo his personal mission, often beating larger forces and terrifying the border.

sentences.zh: 大統西年，為其長史楊伯蘭所害。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Datong he was killed by his chief clerk Yang Bolan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Datong his chief clerk Yang Bolan murdered him.

sentences.zh: 贈司空。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子人傑，有祖、父風。

translations.literal: His son Renjie had the style of his grandfather and father.
translations.idiomatic: His son Renjie inherited the family temper.

sentences.zh: 官至開府儀同三司，改封潁川郡公。

translations.literal: He rose to Director with the ceremonial privileges of the Third Rank and his fief was changed to Duke of Yingchuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He became Director with the ceremonial standing of the Third Rank and was made Duke of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 韋祐，字法保，京兆山北人也，以字行。

translations.literal: Wei You, style name Fabao, was a native of Shanbei in Jingzhao; he was known by his style.
translations.idiomatic: Wei You, styled Fabao, came from Shanbei in Jingzhao and was known by that name.

sentences.zh: 為州郡著姓，父義，上洛郡守。

translations.literal: His clan was a leading family of the province and commandery; his father Yi was Administrator of Shangluo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Weis were a leading clan; his father Yi had been Administrator of Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 魏大統中，以法保著勳，追贈秦州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Datong era of Great Wei, because Fabao's achievements were outstanding, Yi was posthumously granted Governor of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei Datong, for Fabao's merit, Yi was posthumously made Governor of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 法保少好遊俠，而質直少言，所與交遊，皆輕猾亡命。

translations.literal: Fabao in youth loved roaming as a knight-errant yet was plain and spoke little; those he befriended were all reckless men outside the law.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved adventure yet was plain-spoken; his companions were daredevils and outlaws.

sentences.zh: 父沒，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: After his father's death he served his mother with filial piety that won renown.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he mourned his mother with famed filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 慕李長壽之為人，遂娶其女，因寓居闕南。

translations.literal: He admired Li Changshou's conduct, married his daughter, and therefore lived south of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Admiring Li Changshou, he married his daughter and settled south of the passes.

sentences.zh: 正光末，王公避難者或依之，多得全濟，以此為貴遊所德。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenguang many nobles fleeing hardship relied on him and were mostly preserved—therefore the great and powerful were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhenguang many refugees sheltered with him and were saved; the elite owed him gratitude.

sentences.zh: 及孝武西遷，法保赴行在所，封固安縣男。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Fabao went to the traveling palace and was enfeoffed as Baron of Gu'an county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Fabao joined the court and was enfeoffed Baron of Gu'an.

sentences.zh: 及長壽被害，其子延孫收長壽余眾，守禦東境。

translations.literal: When Changshou was killed, his son Yansun gathered the remaining troops and defended the eastern marches.
translations.idiomatic: After Changshou's death his son Yansun took the remnant force to hold the east.

sentences.zh: 朝廷恐延孫兵少，乃除法保東洛州刺史，配兵數百，以援延孫。

translations.literal: The court feared Yansun had too few men and therefore appointed Fabao Governor of Eastern Luozhou with several hundred troops to reinforce him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Yansun was too weak, the court made Fabao Governor of Eastern Luozhou with hundreds of men to aid him.

sentences.zh: 法保至潼關，弘農郡守韋孝寬謂曰：「恐子此役，難以吉還。」

translations.literal: When Fabao reached Tong Pass, Hongnong commandery Administrator Wei Xiaokuan told him, "I fear this expedition of yours will be hard to return from in good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Pass, Wei Xiaokuan warned him, "I fear you may not come back whole from this march.

sentences.zh: 法保曰：「古人稱不入獸穴，不得獸子。

translations.literal: Fabao said, "The ancients said that one who does not enter the beast's den will not capture the cub.
translations.idiomatic: Fabao answered, "As the ancients said, you cannot take the cub without entering the den.

sentences.zh: 安危之事，未可預量。」

translations.literal: Matters of safety and danger cannot be reckoned in advance."
translations.idiomatic: Whether one lives or dies cannot be foretold."

sentences.zh: 遂倍道兼行。

translations.literal: He therefore pressed on at double speed.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on at forced march.

sentences.zh: 與延孫兵接，乃並勢置柵於伏流。

translations.literal: He joined Yansun's troops and together they set palisades at Fuliou.
translations.idiomatic: He united with Yansun and together they fortified Fuliou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，周文追法保與延孫還朝，賞勞甚厚。

translations.literal: Before long Yuwen Tai recalled Fabao and Yansun to court and rewarded them very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuwen Tai recalled both men to court and rewarded them richly.

sentences.zh: 除河南尹。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 及延孫被害，法保乃率所部據延孫舊柵。

translations.literal: When Yansun was killed, Fabao led his own troops and held Yansun's old palisade.
translations.idiomatic: After Yansun's death Fabao held the old camp with his own men.

sentences.zh: 嘗與東魏戰。

translations.literal: He once fought Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Eastern Wei more than once.

sentences.zh: 流矢中頸，從口中出，久之乃蘇。

translations.literal: A stray arrow struck his neck and passed out through his mouth; only after a long while did he revive.
translations.idiomatic: An arrow pierced his neck and exited his mouth; he lay long unconscious before waking.

sentences.zh: 大統九年，鎮九曲城。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Datong he garrisoned Nine-Bend City.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Datong he garrisoned Nine-Bend City.

sentences.zh: 乃侯景以豫州附，法保率兵赴。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing offered Yuzhou in submission, Fabao led troops to go to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing submitted Yuzhou, Fabao marched to join him.

sentences.zh: 景欲留之，法保疑其貳，乃固辭還所鎮。

translations.literal: Jing wished to detain him, but Fabao suspected disloyalty and firmly declined, returning to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Jing tried to keep him, but Fabao distrusted his loyalty and returned to his command.

sentences.zh: 十五年，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，尋進爵為公。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was additionally made General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry and Director with the ceremonial privileges of the Third Rank, and soon was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he became General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry and Director with the ceremonial standing of the Third Rank, then duke.

sentences.zh: 會東魏遣軍送糧饋宜陽，法保潛邀之，中流矢，卒於陣。

translations.literal: When Eastern Wei sent troops to convoy grain to Yiyang, Fabao ambushed them secretly, was struck by a stray arrow, and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Wei convoyed grain to Yiyang, Fabao ambushed them, took an arrow, and died on the field.

sentences.zh: 諡曰莊。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He received the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子初嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chu succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chu inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 位開府儀同大將軍、閻韓防主。

translations.literal: He held the rank of Grand Director with the ceremonial standing of a great general and was chief of Yanhan defense.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Director with the ceremonial rank of a great general and commanded Yanhan defense.

sentences.zh: 陳欣，字永怡，宜陽人也。

translations.literal: Chen Xin, style name Yongyi, was a native of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xin, whose style was Yongyi, came from Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 少驍勇，有氣俠，姿貌魁岸，同類咸敬憚之。

translations.literal: In youth he was fierce and brave, chivalrous in spirit, of imposing stature; his peers all respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was bold, chivalrous, and imposing; his peers feared and respected him.

sentences.zh: 孝武西遷後，欣乃於辟惡山招集勇敢少年，寇掠東魏，仍密遣使歸附。

translations.literal: After Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Xin gathered daring youths on Pibad Mountain, raided Eastern Wei, and secretly sent envoys to submit.
translations.idiomatic: After the western move he rallied bold youths on Pibad Mountain, raided Eastern Wei, and secretly pledged loyalty to the west.

sentences.zh: 授立義大都督，賜爵霸城縣男。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Commander Who Raises Righteousness and enfeoffed as Baron of Bacheng county.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Commander Who Raises Righteousness and Baron of Bacheng.

sentences.zh: 累遷宜陽郡守。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Administrator of Yiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Administrator of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 恭帝二年，進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中、宜陽邑大中正，賜姓尉遲氏。

translations.literal: In the second year of Gongdi he was advanced to General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry and Director with the ceremonial privileges of the Third Rank, additionally made Palace Attendant and Chief Rectifier of Yiyang district, and granted the surname Yuchi.
translations.idiomatic: In Gongdi's second year he became General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, Director with the ceremonial standing of the Three Excellencies, Palace Attendant, and received the surname Yuchi.

sentences.zh: 周文以欣著績累載，贈其祖昆及父興孫俱為儀同三司，位刺史。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai, because Xin had achieved merit over many years, posthumously granted his grandfather Kun and his father Xingsun the ceremonial privileges of the Third Rank and the rank of governor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai posthumously honored his grandfather Kun and father Xingsun as Directors of the Third Rank with gubernatorial rank for Xin's long service.

sentences.zh: 東魏洛州刺史獨孤永業，號有智謀，往來境上，欣與韓雄等恆令間諜覘其動靜，齊兵每至，輒破之，故永業深憚欣等，不敢為寇。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei's Governor of Luozhou Dugu Yongye was famed for strategy and constantly crossed the border; Xin together with Han Xiong always sent spies to watch his movements, and whenever Qi troops came they were beaten—therefore Yongye deeply feared Xin and the others and dared not raid.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou's Dugu Yongye was a clever foe on the border; Xin and Han Xiong used spies and broke every Qi attack, so Yongye feared them and held back.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，進爵許昌縣公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, Xin was advanced to Duke of Xuchang county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Xin was made Duke of Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 後除熊州刺史，卒于州。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Xiongzhou and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Governor of Xiongzhou and died there.

sentences.zh: 欣與韓雄里閈姻婭，少相親昵，俱總兵境上三十餘載。

translations.literal: Xin and Han Xiong were neighbors linked by marriage and from youth were intimate; both commanded troops on the frontier for more than thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: Xin and Han Xiong were kin by marriage, close from youth, and held the frontier together for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 每禦扞，二人相赴，常若影響。

translations.literal: Whenever they defended the border the two rushed to each other's aid, constant as shadow to form.
translations.idiomatic: In every defense they rushed to each other like shadow to body.

sentences.zh: 故數對勍敵，而常保功名。

translations.literal: Therefore, though they often faced strong enemies, they constantly preserved fame and merit.
translations.idiomatic: Though they met fierce foes again and again, they kept their fame and rewards.

sentences.zh: 雖並有武力，至於挽強射中，欣不如雄；

translations.literal: Though both possessed martial strength, in drawing the strong bow and hitting the mark Xin was not the equal of Xiong;
translations.idiomatic: Both were warriors, but in archery Xin fell short of Xiong;

sentences.zh: 散財施惠，得士眾心，則雄不如欣。

translations.literal: in scattering wealth and showing kindness to win the hearts of troops and people, Xiong was not the equal of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: in winning men's hearts with gifts and grace, Xiong fell short of Xin.

sentences.zh: 身死之日，將吏荷其恩德，莫不感慟。

translations.literal: On the day of his death the officers and men, bearing his kindness in mind, were all moved to grief.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his officers and men mourned him for his kindness.

sentences.zh: 子萬敵嗣。

translations.literal: His son Wandi succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wandi inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以欣雅得士心，還令萬敵領其部曲。

translations.literal: The court, because Xin had truly won the hearts of the troops, ordered Wandi to lead his father's forces.
translations.idiomatic: The court let Wandi keep his father's command because Xin had won the soldiers' loyalty.

sentences.zh: 泉仚，字思道，上洛豐陽人也。

translations.literal: Quan Xian, style name Sidao, was a native of Fengyang in Shangluo.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Xian, whose style was Sidao, came from Fengyang in Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 世雄商洛，自晉東度，常貢屬江東。

translations.literal: For generations his clan had been powerful in Shang and Luo; since the Eastern Jin crossing east they had regularly offered tribute to the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had dominated Shang and Luo for generations; since the Eastern Jin crossing they had paid tribute south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 曾祖景言，魏太延五年率鄉里歸化，仍引王師平商洛。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jingyan in the fifth year of Taiyan of Wei led the district in submission and also guided the royal army to pacify Shang and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandfather Jingyan submitted with his district in Wei Taiyan's fifth year and guided the imperial army to pacify Shang and Luo.

sentences.zh: 拜建節將軍，假宜陽郡守，世襲本縣令，封丹水侯。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Establishes Authority, acting Administrator of Yiyang commandery, hereditary magistrate of his home county, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Danshui.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Establishes Authority, acting Administrator of Yiyang, hereditary magistrate of his county, and Marquis of Danshui.

sentences.zh: 父安志，復為建節將軍、宜陽郡守，領本縣令，降爵為伯。

translations.literal: His father Anzhi again became General Who Establishes Authority and Administrator of Yiyang commandery, holding the hereditary magistracy, with his rank reduced to earl.
translations.idiomatic: His father Anzhi held the same posts with hereditary magistracy, at the reduced rank of earl.

sentences.zh: 仚九歲喪父，哀毀類于成人。

translations.literal: Xian at nine sui lost his father and mourned with a grief like an adult's.
translations.idiomatic: Xian lost his father at nine and mourned like a grown man.

sentences.zh: 服闋襲爵，年十二，鄉人皇平、陳合等三百餘人詣州，請仚為縣令。
