translations.literal: When mourning ended he inherited the enfeoffment; at twelve, fellow townsmen Huang Ping, Chen He, and more than three hundred others went to the province asking that Xian be made magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve, after mourning, three hundred locals petitioned the province to make him magistrate.

sentences.zh: 州為申上。

translations.literal: The province reported it upward.
translations.idiomatic: The province forwarded the petition.

sentences.zh: 時吏部尚書郭祚以仚年少，請別選遣，終此一限，令仚代之。

translations.literal: At that time Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Guo Zuo, because Xian was young, asked to send another choice for the moment and let Xian replace him when the term ended.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Guo Zuo, thinking him too young, asked to appoint another for one term and let Xian follow.

sentences.zh: 宣武詔依皇平等所請。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu issued an edict granting what Huang Ping and the others had requested.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu decreed that Huang Ping's petition be granted.

sentences.zh: 巴俗事道，尤重老子之術。

translations.literal: The customs of Ba serve the Way, especially honoring the art of Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Ba practiced the Way and held Laozi's teachings in special esteem.

sentences.zh: 仚雖童幼，而好學恬靜，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Although Xian was still a child, he loved learning and was tranquil, and the common people were at ease under him.
translations.idiomatic: Though still a boy, Xian was studious and calm, and the people were content.

sentences.zh: 尋以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he left office because of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 縣中父老復表請起復本任。

translations.literal: The elders of the county again submitted a memorial asking that he resume his former post before mourning ended.
translations.idiomatic: County elders petitioned again for him to return to office before mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 後除上洛郡守。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Administrator of Shangluo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Administrator of Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 及蕭寶夤反，遣兵趣青泥，圖取上洛，豪族泉、杜二姓密應之。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin rebelled, he sent troops toward Qingni intending to take Shangluo; the great clans Quan and Du secretly responded.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin rebelled and sent troops toward Qingni to seize Shangluo, the powerful Quan and Du clans secretly rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 仚與刺史董紹掩襲，二姓散走，寶夤亦退。

translations.literal: Xian together with Inspector Dong Shao launched a surprise attack; the two clans scattered and fled, and Baoyin also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xian and Inspector Dong Shao struck by surprise; the two clans fled and Baoyin retreated.

sentences.zh: 遷淅州刺史，別封涇陽縣伯。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Inspector of Xizhou and separately enfeoffed as Earl of Jingyang county.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Inspector of Xizhou and separately made Earl of Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 永安中，大破梁將王玄真于順陽，除東雍州刺史，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era he routed Liang general Wang Xuanzhen at Shunyang, was appointed Inspector of Eastern Yongzhou, and advanced in rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: During Yong'an he routed Liang general Wang Xuanzhen at Shunyang, became Inspector of Eastern Yongzhou, and was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 部人楊羊皮，太保椿之從弟，恃椿，侵擾百姓。

translations.literal: A man of the district named Yang Yangpi, a younger cousin of Grand Mentor Chun, relied on Chun and harassed the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yangpi of the district, a cousin of Grand Mentor Chun, relied on Chun's backing to bully the people.

sentences.zh: 守宰多被其陵侮，皆畏而不敢言。

translations.literal: Many local officials were humiliated by him; all feared him and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials whom he browbeat feared him and kept silent.

sentences.zh: 仚收之，將加極法。

translations.literal: Xian arrested him and was about to impose the harshest penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Xian had him arrested and was ready to execute him.

sentences.zh: 楊氏慚懼，闔宗請恩。

translations.literal: The Yang clan, ashamed and afraid, begged mercy for the whole lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed and terrified, the Yang clan pleaded for the whole family's lives.

sentences.zh: 自此豪右無敢犯者。

translations.literal: From then on none of the powerful dared to offend.
translations.idiomatic: After that no local bully dared transgress.

sentences.zh: 性又清約，纖毫不擾於人。

translations.literal: His character was also pure and frugal; he did not trouble people in the slightest.
translations.idiomatic: He was also frugal and scrupulous, never troubling people for the least thing.

sentences.zh: 在州五年，每于鄉里運米自給。

translations.literal: During five years in the province he each time hauled rice from his home district to supply himself.
translations.idiomatic: For five years in office he brought his own rice from home.

sentences.zh: 梁魏興郡與洛州接壤，表請內屬。

translations.literal: Liang's Weixing commandery bordered Luozhou and submitted a memorial requesting to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Weixing commandery, bordering Luozhou, petitioned to submit to Wei.

sentences.zh: 詔仚為行台尚書以撫納之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Xian Acting Secretariat Director of the Mobile Office to soothe and receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was ordered as Mobile Office Secretariat Director to win them over.

sentences.zh: 大行台賀拔嶽以仚昔蒞東雍，為吏人所懷，乃表仚復為刺史。

translations.literal: Great Mobile Office Director Heba Yue, because Xian had formerly governed Eastern Yong and was missed by officials and commoners, memorialized that Xian again be made Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Yue, noting Xian's popularity from his Eastern Yong tenure, petitioned to restore him as Inspector.

sentences.zh: 詔許之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 蜀人張國俊聚黨剽劫，州郡不能制，仚收戮之，闔境清肅。

translations.literal: Shu man Zhang Guojun gathered a band for pillage; the province and commanderies could not control him. Xian arrested and executed him, and the whole territory was cleared and ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guojun of Shu led bandits the province could not restrain; Xian captured and executed him, and the region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武專政，孝武有西顧之心，欲委仚以山南之事，乃除洛州刺史。

translations.literal: When Qi Shenwu seized power, Emperor Xiaowu turned his gaze westward and wished to entrust Xian with affairs south of the mountains, and so appointed him Inspector of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: As Qi Shenwu dominated the court, Emperor Xiaowu looked west and entrusted Xian with the southern mountains, making him Inspector of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，帝西遷。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor moved west.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor fled west.

sentences.zh: 齊神武率眾至潼關，仚遣其子元禮禦之，神武不敢進。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu led his host to Tong Pass; Xian sent his son Yuanli to resist, and Shenwu dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Shenwu marched on Tong Pass, Xian sent Yuanli to block him and Shenwu did not advance.

sentences.zh: 上洛人都督泉岳，其弟猛略與拒陽人杜窋等謀翻洛州以應東魏。

translations.literal: Quan Yue, Area Commander of Shangluo, and his brother Menglue together with Du Qiu of Juyang and others plotted to overturn Luozhou in response to Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Area Commander Quan Yue of Shangluo and his brother Menglue plotted with Du Qiu of Juyang to turn Luozhou to Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 仚知之，殺嶽及猛略，傳首詣闕。

translations.literal: Xian learned of it, killed Yue and Menglue, and sent their heads to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xian uncovered the plot, executed Yue and Menglue, and sent their heads to court.

sentences.zh: 大統元年，加開府儀同三司，兼尚書右僕射，進爵上洛郡公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong he was given the additional titles of General with Honored Appointment of the First Order and Concurrent Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, and advanced to Duke of Shangluo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 1 he was made General with Honored Appointment, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Duke of Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 仚志尚廉慎，每除一官，憂見顏色，寢食輒減。

translations.literal: Xian's aspiration was purity and caution; each time he received an appointment worry showed on his face and his sleep and food were at once reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Xian valued integrity; each new appointment weighed on him and he ate and slept less.

sentences.zh: 至是頻讓，魏帝手詔不許。

translations.literal: On this occasion he repeatedly declined, and the Wei emperor's personal edict would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly declined, but the emperor's personal edict refused to accept.

sentences.zh: 三年，高敖曹圍逼州城，杜窋為其鄉導。

translations.literal: In the third year Gao Aocao besieged the provincial city; Du Qiu served as his guide.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 Gao Aocao besieged the city with Du Qiu as guide.

sentences.zh: 仚拒守旬餘，矢盡援絕，城乃陷焉。

translations.literal: Xian defended for more than ten days; when arrows were exhausted and relief cut off, the city then fell.
translations.idiomatic: Xian held out ten-odd days until arrows and relief ran out and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 謂敖曹曰：「泉仚力屈，志不服也。」

translations.literal: He said to Aocao: "Quan Xian's strength is spent, but his will does not submit.
translations.idiomatic: He told Aocao, "Quan Xian's strength is broken, but his will is not.

sentences.zh: 及竇泰被禽，敖曹退走，遂執仚而東，以窋為刺史。

translations.literal: When Dou Tai was captured, Aocao withdrew; then they seized Xian and took him east, and made Qiu Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: After Dou Tai was captured and Aocao withdrew, they took Xian east and installed Du Qiu as Inspector.

sentences.zh: 仚臨發，密戒二子元禮、仲遵曰：「吾生平志願，不過令長，幸逢聖會，位亞台司。

translations.literal: As Xian was about to depart, he secretly admonished his two sons Yuanli and Zhongzun, saying: "My life's aspiration was no more than magistrate or chief; fortunately meeting a sage age, my rank stood next to the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving, Xian privately told Yuanli and Zhongzun: "I never aspired beyond district office; by fortune I rose near the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 今爵祿既隆，年齒又暮，前途夷險，抑亦可知。

translations.literal: Now rank and salary are already lofty and my years are old; whether the road ahead is smooth or perilous can likewise be known.
translations.idiomatic: My rank and years are high; what lies ahead is plain enough.

sentences.zh: 汝等堪立功效，不得以我在東，遂虧臣節也，」乃揮涕而訣。

translations.literal: You are capable of establishing merit; you must not because I am in the east then fail in your duty as subjects." Then he waved tears and took leave.
translations.idiomatic: "Prove yourselves in service—do not fail your duty because I am captive in the east." He wept and bade farewell.

sentences.zh: 聞者莫不憤歎。

translations.literal: Those who heard it none failed to feel indignant grief.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard wept with indignation.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於鄴。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died at Ye.

sentences.zh: 元禮少有志氣，好弓馬，頗閑草隸，有士君子之風。

translations.literal: Yuanli from youth had ambition and spirit, loved archery and horsemanship, was quite skilled in draft and clerical script, and had the bearing of a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli was spirited from youth, skilled in arms and calligraphy, and carried himself as a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 賜爵臨洮縣伯，散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was granted the rank of Earl of Lintao county and made Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Riders.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Earl of Lintao and Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Riders.

sentences.zh: 及洛州陷，與仚俱被執而東。

translations.literal: When Luozhou fell he was seized together with Xian and taken east.
translations.idiomatic: When Luozhou fell he was captured with Xian and taken east.

sentences.zh: 元禮于路逃歸。

translations.literal: Yuanli escaped on the road and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli escaped en route and returned home.

sentences.zh: 時杜窋雖為刺史，然巴人素輕杜而重泉。

translations.literal: Although Du Qiu was then Inspector, the people of Ba had long held Du lightly and esteemed the Quan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Though Du Qiu held the post, the Ba people respected the Quans far more than him.

sentences.zh: 及元禮至，與仲遵相見，感父臨別之言，潛與豪右結托，遂率鄉人襲州城，斬窋，傳首長安。

translations.literal: When Yuanli arrived and met Zhongzun, moved by their father's parting words they secretly joined with the powerful gentry, then led their countrymen in storming the provincial city, beheaded Qiu, and sent his head to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli reunited with Zhongzun, heeded their father's charge, rallied local power, stormed the city, killed Du Qiu, and sent his head to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，代襲洛州刺史。

translations.literal: The court praised this and allowed him to inherit the post of Inspector of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court rewarded him with the Luozhou inspectorship.

sentences.zh: 從周文戰于沙苑，中流矢卒。

translations.literal: Following Zhou Wen he fought at Shuyuan, was struck by a flying arrow, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Shuyuan, struck by an arrow in Zhou Wen's service.

sentences.zh: 子貞嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhen succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 仲遵一名恭。

translations.literal: Zhongzun had another name, Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzun was also known as Gong.

sentences.zh: 少謹實，涉獵經史。

translations.literal: From youth he was prudent and solid, and ranged through the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was earnest and well read in the classics.

sentences.zh: 年十三為郡主簿，十四為縣令。

translations.literal: At thirteen he became Chief Clerk of the commandery; at fourteen, magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he was commandery chief clerk; at fourteen, magistrate.

sentences.zh: 及長，有武藝。

translations.literal: When he grew up he had martial skill.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he proved able in arms.

sentences.zh: 高敖曹攻洛州，與仚力戰拒守。

translations.literal: When Gao Aocao attacked Luozhou he fought fiercely with Xian in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Aocao besieged Luozhou he fought beside Xian to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 矢盡，以棒杖扞之，為流矢中目，不堪復戰。

translations.literal: When arrows were exhausted he used clubs to beat them off; a stray arrow struck his eye and he could no longer fight.
translations.idiomatic: Out of arrows, he beat back the assault with clubs until a stray shot blinded him.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，士卒歎曰：「若二郎不傷，豈至於此！」

translations.literal: When the city fell the soldiers sighed: "If the Second Lord had not been wounded, how could it have come to this!
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell the troops mourned: "Had the Second Lord not been wounded, we would not have fallen!

sentences.zh: 仚之東也，仲遵以被傷不行。

translations.literal: When Xian was taken east, Zhongzun because of his wound did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian was taken east, Zhongzun stayed behind, too wounded to travel.

sentences.zh: 後與元禮斬窋，以功封豐陽縣伯，東豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Later together with Yuanli he beheaded Qiu; for merit he was enfeoffed Earl of Fengyang county and made Inspector of Eastern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yuanli later killed Du Qiu and he was made Earl of Fengyang and Inspector of Eastern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 及元禮戰沒，復以仲遵為洛州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yuanli fell in battle Zhongzun was again made Inspector of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanli's death he succeeded him as Inspector of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 頗得譽。

translations.literal: He gained considerable praise.
translations.idiomatic: He won a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 大統十三年，行荊州刺史事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Datong he acted as Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 13 he served as acting Inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 梁司州刺史柳仲禮每為邊寇，周文令仲遵率鄉兵，從開府楊忠討之。

translations.literal: Liang Inspector of Sizhou Liu Zhongli often raided the border; Zhou Wen ordered Zhongzun to lead local troops and follow General with Honored Appointment Yang Zhong to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhongli of Liang raided the border; Zhou Wen sent Zhongzun with local levies under Yang Zhong against him.

sentences.zh: 梁隨郡守桓和拒守不降。

translations.literal: Liang Administrator of Suí commandery Huan He defended and would not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Huan He, Liang's Suí commandery chief, held out and refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 忠謂諸將曰：「先取仲禮，則桓和不攻而自服也。」

translations.literal: Zhong said to the generals: "If we first take Zhongli, then Huan He without attack will submit of himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong told his officers: "Take Zhongli first and Huan He will surrender without a fight.

sentences.zh: 仲遵對曰：「若棄和深入，仲禮未即就禽，則首尾受敵，此危道也。」

translations.literal: Zhongzun replied: "If we abandon He and push deep, and Zhongli is not immediately captured, then we will be attacked front and rear—this is a perilous course."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzun answered: "Bypass Huan He and we risk being caught between two enemies before Zhongli falls—that is perilous."

sentences.zh: 忠從之。

translations.literal: Zhong followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong took his advice.

sentences.zh: 仲遵以計由已出，乃先登城，遂禽和。

translations.literal: Zhongzun, because the plan came from himself, then was first to scale the wall and thus captured He.
translations.idiomatic: As the plan was his, Zhongzun led the assault that captured Huan He.

sentences.zh: 從擊仲禮，又獲之。

translations.literal: Following up the attack on Zhongli he again captured him.
translations.idiomatic: He then helped capture Liu Zhongli as well.

sentences.zh: 進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、本州大中正，復行荊州刺史、十三州諸軍事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General of Chariots and Cavalry, General with Honored Appointment of the First Order, and Chief Rectifier of his native province; again acting Inspector of Jingzhou and commander of military affairs of thirteen provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Honored Appointment, made Chief Rectifier and acting Inspector of Jingzhou over thirteen provinces.

sentences.zh: 尋遭母憂，請終喪制，不許。

translations.literal: Soon he suffered mourning for his mother and asked to complete the full mourning term; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he asked to finish full mourning but was refused.

sentences.zh: 大將軍王雄南征上津、魏興，仲遵從雄討平之。

translations.literal: Great General Wang Xiong campaigned south against Shangjin and Weixing; Zhongzun followed Xiong and subdued them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzun joined Wang Xiong's southern campaign and helped pacify Shangjin and Weixing.

sentences.zh: 遂于上津置南洛州，以仲遵為刺史。

translations.literal: Then at Shangjin they established Southern Luozhou and made Zhongzun its Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Luozhou was established at Shangjin with Zhongzun as Inspector.

sentences.zh: 仲遵留情撫接，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Zhongzun with care soothed and received them, and the common people were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzun governed with care and won the people's peace.

sentences.zh: 初，蠻帥杜青和自稱巴州刺史，以州入附，朝遷因其所據而授之，仍隸東梁州都督。

translations.literal: Initially the Man chieftain Du Qinghe styled himself Inspector of Bazhou and submitted the province; the court, following what he held, appointed him and still placed him under the Area Commander of Eastern Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Man chieftain Du Qinghe had submitted as Bazhou Inspector and was left under Eastern Liangzhou's command.

sentences.zh: 青和以仲遵善於撫禦，請隸仲遵。

translations.literal: Qinghe, because Zhongzun was skilled at soothing and governing, asked to be placed under Zhongzun.
translations.idiomatic: Du Qinghe asked to transfer to Zhongzun's jurisdiction for his fair rule.

sentences.zh: 朝議以山川非便，弗之許也。

translations.literal: Court deliberation held the mountains and rivers inconvenient and did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused, citing the awkward terrain.

sentences.zh: 青和遂結安康酋帥黃眾寶等，舉兵共圍東梁州。

translations.literal: Qinghe then joined with the chieftain of Ankang Huang Zhongbao and others, raised troops and together besieged Eastern Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du Qinghe then allied with Huang Zhongbao of Ankang and besieged Eastern Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 復遣王雄討平之，改巴州為洵州，隸于仲遵。

translations.literal: Wang Xiong was again sent to suppress and pacify them; Bazhou was changed to Xunzhou and placed under Zhongzun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiong crushed the revolt; Bazhou became Xunzhou under Zhongzun.

sentences.zh: 先是東梁刺史劉孟良在職貪婪，人多背叛。

translations.literal: Previously Eastern Liang Inspector Liu Mengliang in office was greedy; many people rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Former inspector Liu Mengliang's greed had driven many to rebel.

sentences.zh: 仲遵以廉簡處之，群蠻帥服。

translations.literal: Zhongzun with integrity and simplicity handled affairs, and the Man chieftains submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzun's clean rule won the Man chiefs' submission.

sentences.zh: 仲遵雖出自巴夷，而有方雅之操，曆官之處，皆以清白見稱。

translations.literal: Although Zhongzun came from the Ba tribes, he had refined and elegant bearing; in every office he was praised for purity.
translations.idiomatic: Though of Ba tribal descent, Zhongzun was refined; every post he held was noted for integrity.

sentences.zh: 朝廷又以其父臨危抗節，乃令襲爵上洛郡公，舊封聽回授一子。

translations.literal: The court also because his father at peril resisted to the end ordered him to inherit the ducal rank of Shangluo commandery; the old enfeoffment was permitted to be transferred back to one son.
translations.idiomatic: For his father's death resisting capture, he inherited the Dukedom of Shangluo and could pass an older title to a son.

sentences.zh: 尋出為都督、金州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Area Commander and Inspector of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Area Commander and Inspector of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍、三州刺史，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Great General and Inspector of three provinces; posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Great General and Inspector of three provinces, with the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子暼恆嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yanheng succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanheng inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 位至開府儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: He reached the rank of General with Honored Appointment of the First Order and Great General.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Honored Appointment and Great General.

sentences.zh: 李遷哲，字孝彥，安康人也。

translations.literal: Li Qianzhe, style name Xiaoyan, was a native of Ankang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qianzhe, whose style was Xiaoyan, came from Ankang.

sentences.zh: 世為山南豪族，仕于江左。

translations.literal: For generations his clan was a powerful family south of the mountains and served in the lands east of the river.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had been a southern-mountain power serving the Yangtze regimes.

sentences.zh: 父元直，仕梁，曆東梁、衡二州刺史、散騎常侍、沌陽侯。

translations.literal: His father Yuanzhi served Liang, successively as Inspector of Eastern Liang and Heng provinces, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Riders, and Marquis of Dünyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanzhi served Liang as inspector of Eastern Liang and Heng, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Marquis of Dünyang.

sentences.zh: 遷哲少修立，有識度，慷慨善謀畫，起家文德主帥。

translations.literal: Qianzhe from youth was upright and established, had insight and breadth, was generous and skilled in planning, and began his career as Commander of Wende.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe was upright and far-sighted from youth, bold in counsel, and entered service as Commander of Wende.

sentences.zh: 其父為衡州，留遷哲本鄉，臨統部曲事。

translations.literal: When his father was at Hengzhou he left Qianzhe in his home district to command the forces locally.
translations.idiomatic: While his father governed Hengzhou, Qianzhe stayed home to command local troops.

sentences.zh: 時年二十，撫馭群下，甚得其情。

translations.literal: At that time he was twenty; in soothing and controlling his subordinates he greatly won their feeling.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he won his men through fair leadership.

sentences.zh: 後襲爵沌陽侯，位都督、東梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he inherited the rank of Marquis of Dünyang and held the posts of Area Commander and Inspector of Eastern Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later inherited the Marquisate of Dünyang and became Area Commander and Eastern Liangzhou Inspector.

sentences.zh: 侯景篡逆，遷哲外禦邊寇，自守而已。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing usurped, Qianzhe outwardly repelled border raiders and merely defended himself.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion Qianzhe held his ground and guarded the border.

sentences.zh: 大統十七年，周文遣達奚武、王雄等略地山南。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Datong Zhou Wen sent Daxi Wu, Wang Xiong, and others to seize territory south of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 17 Zhou Wen sent Daxi Wu and Wang Xiong to conquer the southern mountains.

sentences.zh: 遷哲軍敗，遂降于武。

translations.literal: Qianzhe's army was defeated and he then surrendered to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, Qianzhe surrendered to Daxi Wu.

sentences.zh: 然猶意氣自若。

translations.literal: Yet his spirit remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he carried himself without shame.

sentences.zh: 武乃執送京師。

translations.literal: Wu then seized him and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wu sent him bound to the capital.

sentences.zh: 周文責以不早歸國。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen reproached him for not returning to the realm earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen rebuked him for not submitting sooner.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「不能死節，實以此愧耳。」

translations.literal: He answered: "That I could not die maintaining my integrity—truly I am ashamed for this.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "I am ashamed that I could not die loyal.

sentences.zh: 周文深嘉之，封沌陽縣伯。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen deeply praised this and enfeoffed him as Earl of Dünyang county.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen admired the reply and made him Earl of Dünyang.

sentences.zh: 恭帝初，直州人樂熾、洋州人黃國等連結為亂。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Gongdi reign the men of Zhizhou Le Chi and Huang Guo of Yangzhou and others joined in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: At Gongdi's accession Le Chi of Zhizhou and Huang Guo of Yangzhou raised a revolt.

sentences.zh: 周文以遷哲信著山南，乃令與開府賀若敦同經略。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen, because Qianzhe's trust was established south of the mountains, ordered him together with General with Honored Appointment He Ruo Dun to conduct the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen sent Qianzhe with He Ruo Dun to pacify the south, trusting his local standing.

sentences.zh: 熾等尋並平蕩，仍與敦南出狥地。

translations.literal: Chi and the others were soon pacified; still together with Dun he marched south to extend the territory.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were quickly suppressed, and he marched south with Dun to extend the frontier.

sentences.zh: 遷哲先至巴州，入其封郭。

translations.literal: Qianzhe arrived first at Bazhou and entered its outer walls.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe reached Bazhou first and entered its outer city.

sentences.zh: 梁巴州剌史牟安人開門請降。

translations.literal: Liang Administrator of Bazhou Mou Anren opened the gates and asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Bazhou administrator Mou Anren opened the gates to surrender.

sentences.zh: 安人子宗徹等猶據巴城不下，遷哲攻克之。

translations.literal: Anren's son Zongche and others still held Bazhou city and would not come down; Qianzhe stormed it and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Anren's son Zongche still held the inner city until Qianzhe captured it.

sentences.zh: 軍次鹿城，城主遣使請降。

translations.literal: The army halted at Lucheng; the city chief sent envoys asking to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At Lucheng the garrison sent envoys offering surrender.

sentences.zh: 遷哲謂其眾曰：「納降如受敵，吾觀其使，瞻視猶高，得無詐也？」

translations.literal: Qianzhe said to his troops: "Receiving surrender is like facing the enemy; I see their envoy's gaze is still high—could there not be deceit?
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe told his men: "Surrender must be treated like battle—the envoy's eyes were too proud; this may be a trap.

sentences.zh: 遂不許之。

translations.literal: He then did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the offer.

sentences.zh: 梁人果于道左設伏以邀遷哲，遷哲進擊破之，遂屠其城。

translations.literal: The Liang men indeed set an ambush on the road to intercept Qianzhe; Qianzhe advanced, attacked, and broke them, then slaughtered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liang forces ambushed the road; Qianzhe routed them and sacked the city.

sentences.zh: 自此巴、濮之人，降款相繼。

translations.literal: From then on the people of Ba and Pu submitted in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Ba and Pu peoples submitted one after another.

sentences.zh: 軍還，周文賜以所服紫袍玉帶及所乘馬，加授侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，除真州刺史，即本州也。

translations.literal: When the army returned Zhou Wen bestowed on him the purple robe and jade belt he himself wore and the horse he rode, and additionally appointed him Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Chariots and Cavalry, General with Honored Appointment of the First Order, and Inspector of Zhenzhou—the very province of his origin.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Zhou Wen gave him his own purple robe, jade belt, and mount, and made him Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Honored Appointment, and Inspector of his native Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 仍給軍儀鼓節，令與田弘同討信州。

translations.literal: He was also given military banners, drums, and credentials, and ordered together with Tian Hong to attack Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was given full military insignia and ordered with Tian Hong to attack Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 時信州為蠻酋向五子王等所圍，弘遣遷哲赴援。

translations.literal: At that time Xinzhou was besieged by the Man chieftains Xiang Wuzi Wang and others; Hong sent Qianzhe to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzhou was besieged by Man chiefs led by Xiang Wuzi Wang; Hong sent Qianzhe to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 此至，信州已陷。

translations.literal: When he arrived Xinzhou had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived Xinzhou had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 五子王等聞遷哲至，狼狽遁走。

translations.literal: Wuzi Wang and the others, hearing Qianzhe had come, fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Qianzhe was near, Wuzi Wang and the others fled in disarray.

sentences.zh: 遷哲入據白帝，賀若敦等復至，遂共追五子王等，破之。

translations.literal: Qianzhe entered and held Baidi; He Ruo Dun and others also arrived, and together they pursued Wuzi Wang and the others and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe seized Baidi; Dun joined him and they routed Wuzi Wang's forces.

sentences.zh: 及田弘旋軍，周文令遷哲留鎮白帝。

translations.literal: When Tian Hong withdrew Zhou Wen ordered Qianzhe to remain and garrison Baidi.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Hong withdrew, Zhou Wen left Qianzhe to hold Baidi.

sentences.zh: 信州先無倉儲，軍糧匱乏。

translations.literal: Xinzhou had previously had no granaries, and army provisions were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzhou had no stores and the army was starving.

sentences.zh: 遷哲乃收葛根造粉，兼米以給之，遷哲亦自取供食。

translations.literal: Qianzhe then gathered kudzu roots to make flour and mixed it with rice to supply them; Qianzhe also took from this for his own food.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe ground kudzu into flour, mixed it with rice for the troops, and ate the same himself.

sentences.zh: 時有異膳，即分賜兵士。

translations.literal: When there was special fare he at once divided and bestowed it on the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Any special food he received he shared with the men.

sentences.zh: 有疾患者，又親加醫藥。

translations.literal: When there were sick he personally added medicine.
translations.idiomatic: He personally tended the sick.

sentences.zh: 以此軍中感之，人思效命。

translations.literal: Because of this the army was moved by him and each man wished to give his life.
translations.idiomatic: The army was deeply moved and eager to fight for him.

sentences.zh: 黔陽蠻田烏度、田烏唐，等每抄掠江中，為百姓患。

translations.literal: The Qianyang Man Tian Wudu and Tian Wutang and others constantly raided the river and were a affliction to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyang Man chiefs Tian Wudu and Tian Wutang raided the river and terrorized the people.

sentences.zh: 遷哲隨機出討，殺討甚多，由是諸蠻畏威，各送糧餼。

translations.literal: Qianzhe went out to attack as occasion demanded and killed very many; because of this the various Man feared his might and each sent grain and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe struck them repeatedly, killing many; the Man submitted grain in fear.

sentences.zh: 又遣子弟入質者千有餘家，遷哲乃於白帝城外築城以處之。

translations.literal: More than a thousand families also sent sons and younger brothers as hostages; Qianzhe then built a city outside Baidi to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Over a thousand families sent hostages; Qianzhe built a settlement outside Baidi for them.

sentences.zh: 並置四鎮，以靜峽路。

translations.literal: He also established four garrisons to quiet the gorge route.
translations.idiomatic: He established four garrisons to secure the gorge route.

sentences.zh: 自此寇抄頗息，軍糧贍給焉。

translations.literal: From then on raiding largely ceased and army provisions were supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Raids largely ceased and the army was fed.

sentences.zh: 周明帝初，授都督、信州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Mingdi reign of Zhou he was appointed Area Commander and Inspector of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhou Mingdi's reign he became Area Commander and Inspector of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，進爵西城縣公。

translations.literal: In the second year he advanced in rank to Duke of Xicheng county.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he was raised to Duke of Xicheng.

sentences.zh: 武成元年，朝于京師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wucheng he attended court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Wucheng year 1 he attended court at the capital.

sentences.zh: 明帝甚禮之，賜甲第及莊田等。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming treated him with great ceremony and bestowed a fine mansion and estate lands and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming received him with great honor and granted him a mansion and estates.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe he advanced in rank to Great General.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe year 3 he was promoted to Great General.

sentences.zh: 詔遷哲率金、上等諸州兵鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Qianzhe to lead troops of Jin, Shang, and other provinces to garrison Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to lead troops from Jin, Shang, and other provinces to garrison Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 五年，陳將章昭達攻逼江陵，梁明帝告急於襄州，衛公直令遷哲往救焉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Chen general Zhang Zhaoda pressed Jiangling; Liang Emperor Ming urgently appealed to Xiangzhou, and Duke of Wei Zhi ordered Qianzhe to go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 Chen general Zhang Zhaoda besieged Jiangling; Liang Emperor Ming appealed to Xiangzhou and Duke Zhi sent Qianzhe to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 遷哲率其所部守江陵外城，自率騎出南門，又令步兵自北門出，兩軍首尾邀之，陳人多投水死。

translations.literal: Qianzhe led his own forces to defend the outer wall of Jiangling; he himself led cavalry out the south gate and also ordered infantry out the north gate; the two armies attacked front and rear, and many Chen men drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe held Jiangling's outer wall, sent cavalry out the south gate and infantry out the north, and caught the Chen army front and rear; many drowned.

sentences.zh: 是夜，陳人又竊於城西堞以梯登城，登者已百數人。

translations.literal: That night Chen men again secretly climbed the ramparts on the west with ladders; more than a hundred had already mounted.
translations.idiomatic: That night Chen troops scaled the western wall by ladder; over a hundred had already climbed up.

sentences.zh: 遷哲又率驍勇扞之，陳人復潰。

translations.literal: Qianzhe again led fierce warriors to beat them off, and the Chen men again broke.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe led elite troops to drive them back and the Chen force collapsed again.

sentences.zh: 俄而大風暴起，遷哲乘暗出兵擊其營，陳人大亂，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: Soon a great windstorm arose; Qianzhe in the darkness sent troops to strike their camp, and the Chen men fell into great disorder with very many killed and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: A sudden gale rose; Qianzhe struck the Chen camp in darkness and inflicted heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 江陵總管陸騰復破之於西隄，陳人乃遁。

translations.literal: Jiangling Area Commander Lu Teng again defeated them at the western embankment, and the Chen men then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Area Commander Lu Teng also routed them at the western dike and the Chen army fled.

sentences.zh: 建德二年，進爵安康郡公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiande he advanced in rank to Duke of Ankang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiande year 2 he was raised to Duke of Ankang.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒於襄州。

translations.literal: In the third year he died at Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he died at Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 贈金州總管，諡曰壯武。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Area Commander of Jinzhou; posthumous name Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Area Commander of Jinzhou, with the posthumous name Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 遷哲累葉雄豪，為鄉里所服。

translations.literal: Qianzhe for successive generations was a local power and was obeyed by his home district.
translations.idiomatic: For generations Qianzhe's clan had dominated the countryside.

sentences.zh: 性復華侈，能厚自奉養。

translations.literal: His character was again lavish; he could richly maintain himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was also extravagant and lived in great comfort.

sentences.zh: 妾媵至有百數，男女六十九人。

translations.literal: His concubines reached a hundred in number; sons and daughters sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a hundred concubines and had sixty-nine children.

sentences.zh: 緣漢千餘里間，第宅相次，姬媵之有子者，分處其中，各有僮僕侍婢閽人守護。

translations.literal: Along more than a thousand li beside the Han, mansions stood in succession; concubines who had borne sons each had separate quarters, each with servants, maids, and gatekeepers standing guard.
translations.idiomatic: For over a thousand li along the Han his mansions lined the river; each concubine with a son had her own household with servants and guards.

sentences.zh: 遷哲每鳴笳導從，往來其間，縱酒歡宴，盡生平之樂。

translations.literal: Qianzhe each time sounded pipes and led his retinue, passing back and forth among them, drinking wine and feasting, enjoying to the full the pleasures of his life.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled among them with pipe music and retinue, feasting through the pleasures of a lifetime.

sentences.zh: 子孫參見，或忘其年名者，披簿以審之。

translations.literal: When sons and grandsons came to see him he sometimes forgot their age and names and opened the register to verify.
translations.idiomatic: When sons and grandsons visited he sometimes forgot their names and checked the family register.

sentences.zh: 長子敬仁，先遷哲卒。

translations.literal: The eldest son Jingren died before Qianzhe.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Jingren predeceased him.

sentences.zh: 第六子敬猷嗣，還統父兵，位儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: The sixth son Jingyou succeeded him, returned to command his father's troops, and held the rank of Honored Appointment Great General.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth son Jingyou inherited the line, took command of his father's troops, and rose to Honored Appointment Great General.

sentences.zh: 遷哲弟顯，位上儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: Qianzhe's younger brother Xian held the rank of Senior Honored Appointment Great General.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe's brother Xian rose to Senior Honored Appointment Great General.

sentences.zh: 楊乾運，字玄邈，儻城興勢人也，少雄武，為鄉閭信服。

translations.literal: Yang Ganyun, style name Xuanyao, was a native of Xingshi in Tangcheng; from youth he was bold in martial bearing and was trusted by his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ganyun, whose style was Xuanyao, came from Xingshi in Tangcheng; from youth he was bold and trusted locally.

sentences.zh: 為安康郡守。

translations.literal: He was Administrator of Ankang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Ankang.

sentences.zh: 陷梁，仕歷潼、南梁二州刺史。

translations.literal: When it fell to Liang he served successively as Inspector of Tong and Southern Liang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang took the region he served as Inspector of Tong and Southern Liang.

sentences.zh: 及武陵王蕭紀稱尊號，以乾運威服巴、渝，乃拜梁州刺史，鎮潼州，封萬春縣公。

translations.literal: When Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji assumed the imperial title, because Ganyun's might had subdued Ba and Yu he was appointed Inspector of Liang province, garrisoned Tongzhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wanchun county.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji claimed the throne, Ganyun's sway over Ba and Yu won him the Liang inspectorship, Tongzhou garrison, and Dukedom of Wanchun.

sentences.zh: 時紀與其兄湘東王繹爭帝，乾運兄子略勸乾運歸附，乾運然之。

translations.literal: At that time Ji was contending with his elder brother Prince of Xiangdong Xiao Yi for the throne; Ganyun's elder brother's son Lue urged Ganyun to submit; Ganyun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: As Ji fought his brother Xiao Yi for the throne, Ganyun's nephew Lue urged submission and Ganyun agreed.

sentences.zh: 會周文令乾運孫法洛至，略即夜送之，乾運送款，周文密賜乾運鐵券，授開府儀同三司、侍中、梁州刺史、安康郡公。

translations.literal: When Zhou Wen sent Ganyun's grandson Faluo, Lue that night sent him on; Ganyun sent his pledge of loyalty; Zhou Wen secretly bestowed on Ganyun an iron certificate and appointed him General with Honored Appointment of the First Order, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Inspector of Liang province, and Duke of Ankang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen sent Ganyun's grandson Faluo; Lue forwarded him by night; Ganyun submitted and Zhou Wen secretly granted him an iron certificate and made him Honored Appointment, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Liang Inspector, and Duke of Ankang.

sentences.zh: 及尉遲迥征蜀，遂降迥。

translations.literal: When Yu Chi Jiong campaigned against Shu he then surrendered to Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Chi Jiong marched on Shu, Ganyun surrendered to him.

sentences.zh: 迥因此進軍成都，數旬克之。

translations.literal: Jiong therefore advanced on Chengdu and took it in several tens of days.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong thereby took Chengdu within weeks.

sentences.zh: 及至京師，禮遇隆渥。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital the courtesy and favor were thick and generous.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital he was received with great honor.

sentences.zh: 尋卒于長安。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子端嗣。

translations.literal: His son Duan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duan inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 略亦以歸附功，位至開府儀同三司、大將軍，封上庸縣伯。

translations.literal: Lue also for the merit of submission reached General with Honored Appointment of the First Order and Great General, and was enfeoffed as Earl of Shangyong county.
translations.idiomatic: Lue too rose to Honored Appointment and Great General and was made Earl of Shangyong for his submission.

sentences.zh: 乾運女婿樂廣，安州刺史，封安康縣公

translations.literal: Ganyun's son-in-law Yue Guang, Inspector of Anzhou, was enfeoffed as Duke of Ankang county.
translations.idiomatic: Ganyun's son-in-law Yue Guang, Inspector of Anzhou, was made Duke of Ankang.

sentences.zh: 扶猛，字宗略，上甲黃土人也。

translations.literal: Fu Meng, style name Zonglue, was a native of Huangtu in Shangjia.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Meng, whose style was Zonglue, came from Huangtu in Shangjia.

sentences.zh: 其種落號白獸蠻。

translations.literal: His tribe was called the White Beast Man.
translations.idiomatic: His people were known as the White Beast Man.

sentences.zh: 猛仕梁，位南洛、北司二州刺史，封宕梁縣男。

translations.literal: Meng served Liang, holding the posts of Inspector of Southern Luo and Northern Si provinces and enfeoffed as Baron of Dangliang.
translations.idiomatic: Meng served Liang as Inspector of Southern Luo and Northern Si and Baron of Dangliang.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝元年，以眾降。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Deposed Emperor of Wei he submitted with his host.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei Deposed Emperor year 1 he surrendered with his followers.

sentences.zh: 周文厚加撫納，復爵宕渠縣男，割二郡為羅州，以猛為刺史。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen richly soothed and received him, restored the rank of Baron of Dangqu, carved out two commanderies as Luozhou, and made Meng its Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen welcomed him generously, restored his barony, created Luozhou from two commanderies, and made him its Inspector.

sentences.zh: 令從開府賀若敦南討信州。

translations.literal: He was ordered to follow General with Honored Appointment He Ruo Dun south to attack Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to follow He Ruo Dun south against Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 敦令猛直道白帝，所由之路，人跡不通。

translations.literal: Dun ordered Meng to take the direct route to Baidi; on the road he traveled human tracks did not pass.
translations.idiomatic: Dun sent Meng straight for Baidi by a path where no man had walked.

sentences.zh: 猛乃梯山捫葛，備曆艱阻，遂入白帝。

translations.literal: Meng then scaled mountains and grasped vines, passing through every hardship and peril, and thus entered Baidi.
translations.idiomatic: Meng climbed cliffs and grasped vines through every hardship until he reached Baidi.

sentences.zh: 撫慰人夷。

translations.literal: He soothed both Chinese and tribesmen.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified both settlers and tribesmen.

sentences.zh: 莫不悅附。

translations.literal: None failed to rejoice and attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: All welcomed his rule.

sentences.zh: 以功進開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to General with Honored Appointment of the First Order.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was made General with Honored Appointment.

sentences.zh: 俄則信州蠻反，猛復從賀若敦平之，進爵臨江縣公。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Man of Xinzhou rebelled; Meng again followed He Ruo Dun and pacified them, and advanced in rank to Duke of Linjiang county.
translations.idiomatic: When Xinzhou Man rebelled, Meng again followed Dun to suppress them and was raised to Duke of Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 後從田弘破漢南諸蠻，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: Later he followed Tian Hong and broke the Man south of the Han, and advanced in rank to Great General.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Tian Hong in crushing the southern Han Man and was promoted to Great General.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 陽雄，字元略，上洛邑陽人也。

translations.literal: Yang Xiong, style name Yuanlue, was a native of Yiyang in Shangluo.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong, whose style was Yuanlue, came from Yiyang in Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 累葉豪族。

translations.literal: For generations a powerful clan.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had been powerful for generations.

sentences.zh: 父猛，從孝武西遷，以功封郃陽伯，位征東將軍、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Meng followed Emperor Xiaowu in moving west and for merit was enfeoffed as Earl of Heyang, holding the posts of General Who Conquers the East and Inspector of Yang province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Meng followed Emperor Xiaowu west and was made Earl of Heyang, General Who Conquers the East, and Inspector of Yang.

sentences.zh: 雄起家奉朝請，以軍功封安平縣侯。

translations.literal: Xiong began his career as Bearer of the Court and for military merit was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anping county.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong entered service as Bearer of the Court and was made Marquis of Anping for military merit.

sentences.zh: 得子孫相襲拜邑陽郡守。

translations.literal: He obtained that sons and grandsons in succession might be appointed Administrator of Yiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He won the hereditary right for his line to hold the Yiyang magistracy.

sentences.zh: 累遷平州刺史，進爵玉城縣公，加開府儀同三司、驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted successively to Inspector of Ping province, advanced to Duke of Yucheng county, and given the additional titles of General with Honored Appointment of the First Order and General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Inspector of Ping, Duke of Yucheng, Honored Appointment, and General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 曆京兆尹、戶部中大夫，進位大將軍，轉中外府長史，遷江陵總管，改封魯陽縣公。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Governor of the Capital District, Director of the Households Section, advanced in rank to Great General, transferred to Chief of Staff of the Inner and Outer Offices, moved to Area Commander of Jiangling, and changed enfeoffment to Duke of Luyang county.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Capital Governor, Director of the Households Section, Great General, Chief of Staff, and Area Commander of Jiangling, and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Luyang.

sentences.zh: 卒於鎮。

translations.literal: He died at his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at his post.

sentences.zh: 追封郡公，諡曰懷。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of a commandery; posthumous name Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made a commandery duke with the posthumous name Huai.

sentences.zh: 雄善附會，能自謀身，故任兼出內，保全爵祿。

translations.literal: Xiong was skilled at attaching himself and could look after himself, and therefore held posts both inside and outside the court and preserved rank and salary.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong knew how to align himself and protect his interests, holding posts in and out of court while keeping rank and salary.

sentences.zh: 子長寬嗣。

translations.literal: His son Changkuan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changkuan inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 席固，字子堅，其先安定人也。

translations.literal: Xi Gu, style name Zijian, his ancestors were natives of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Gu, whose style was Zijian, traced his ancestry to Anding.

sentences.zh: 高祖衡，因姚氏之亂，寓居襄陽，仕晉，為建威將軍，遂為襄陽著姓。

translations.literal: High Ancestor Heng, because of the turmoil of the Yao clan, took refuge in Xiangyang, served Jin, and became General Who Establishes Might; thus they became a noted family of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestor Heng fled the Yao turmoil to Xiangyang, served Jin as General Who Establishes Might, and made the Xis a leading Xiangyang clan.

sentences.zh: 固少有遠志。

translations.literal: Gu from youth had far-reaching ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Gu was ambitious from youth.

sentences.zh: 梁大同中，為齊興郡守。

translations.literal: In the Datong era of Liang he was Administrator of Qixing commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang's Datong reign he was Administrator of Qixing.

sentences.zh: 久居郡職，士多附之，遂有親兵千餘人。

translations.literal: Long holding commandery office, many gentlemen attached to him; he then had more than a thousand personal troops.
translations.idiomatic: Long in office he won many followers and raised over a thousand personal troops.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝時，遷興州刺史，軍人募從者至五千餘人。

translations.literal: In the time of Liang Emperor Yuan he was transferred to Inspector of Xing province; soldiers who volunteered to follow reached more than five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang Emperor Yuan he became Inspector of Xing; over five thousand soldiers volunteered to follow him.

sentences.zh: 固欲自據一州，以觀時變。

translations.literal: Gu wished to hold a province for himself and watch how the times changed.
translations.idiomatic: Gu meant to hold a province for himself and wait out the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 大統中，以地歸魏。

translations.literal: In the Datong era he submitted the territory to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the Datong era he submitted his territory to Wei.

sentences.zh: 時周文方南取江陵，西定蜀、漢，聞固至，甚禮遇之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhou Wen was just then taking Jiangling in the south and settling Shu and Han in the west; hearing Gu had come he treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen was conquering Jiangling and settling Shu and Han; on Gu's arrival he received him with great honor.

sentences.zh: 就拜使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、大都督、侍中、豐州刺史，封新豐縣公。

translations.literal: He was at once appointed Bearer of the Staff, General of Chariots and Cavalry, General with Honored Appointment of the First Order, Great Area Commander, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Inspector of Feng province, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xinfeng county.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately made Bearer of the Staff, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Honored Appointment, Great Area Commander, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Inspector of Feng, and Duke of Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 後轉湖州刺史，啟求入觀。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Inspector of Huzhou and memorialized asking to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Inspector of Huzhou and asked to attend court.

sentences.zh: 及至，進爵靜安郡公。

translations.literal: When he arrived he advanced in rank to Duke of Jing'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital he was raised to Duke of Jing'an.

sentences.zh: 尋拜昌、歸、憲三州諸軍事、昌州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed commander of military affairs of Chang, Gui, and Xian provinces and Inspector of Chang province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commander of Chang, Gui, and Xian and Inspector of Chang.

sentences.zh: 固居家孝友，蒞官頗有聲績。

translations.literal: Gu at home was filial and friendly; in office he gained a considerable reputation for achievement.
translations.idiomatic: At home Gu was filial and brotherly; in office he won a solid reputation.

sentences.zh: 卒於州。

translations.literal: He died at his province.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍、五州刺史，諡曰肅，敕襄州賜其墓田。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Great General and Inspector of five provinces; posthumous name Su; an edict from Xiang province granted his tomb lands.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Great General and Inspector of five provinces, with the posthumous name Su; Xiang province granted land for his tomb.

sentences.zh: 子雅嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ya succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ya inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 雅字彥文。

translations.literal: Ya, style name Yanwen.
translations.idiomatic: Ya, whose style was Yanwen.

sentences.zh: 性方正，少以孝聞。

translations.literal: His character was upright and square; from youth he was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Ya was upright and famed from youth for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 位大將軍。

translations.literal: He held the rank of Great General.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Great General.

sentences.zh: 雅弟英，上開府儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: Ya's younger brother Ying held the rank of Senior Honored Appointment Great General.
translations.idiomatic: Ya's brother Ying rose to Senior Honored Appointment Great General.

sentences.zh: 論曰：王傑、王勇、宇文虯、耿豪、高琳、李和、伊婁穆、侯植等咸以果毅之姿，效節擾攘之際，各能屠堅覆銳，自致其功，高爵厚位，固其宜也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Wang Jie, Wang Yong, Yu Wenqiu, Geng Hao, Gao Lin, Li He, Yi Loumu, Hou Zhi, and the like all with a resolute and bold bearing showed loyalty in troubled times; each could slaughter the hard and overturn the sharp and achieve merit by his own effort—high rank and thick emolument were indeed fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Wang Jie, Wang Yong, Yu Wenqiu, Geng Hao, Gao Lin, Li He, Yi Loumu, Hou Zhi, and others—all resolute men who served faithfully in chaos, each cutting through hardened foes to earn high rank and rich reward as they deserved.

sentences.zh: 仲尼稱無求備於一人，信矣。

translations.literal: Confucius said not to expect completeness in a single man—how true!
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said one should not expect perfection in a single man—truly so.

sentences.zh: 夫文士懷溫恭之操，其弊也懦弱；

translations.literal: Literary men cherish a gentle and respectful bearing; their fault is weakness;
translations.idiomatic: Men of letters cherish gentle manners; their failing is timidity;

sentences.zh: 武夫稟剛烈之資，其弊也敢悍。

translations.literal: warriors inherit a fierce and bold nature; their fault is rash violence.
translations.idiomatic: warriors inherit fierce temper; their failing is brutal daring.

sentences.zh: 故有使酒不遜之禍，拔劍爭功之尤，大則莫全其生，小則僅而獲免。

translations.literal: Hence there are the calamities of insolence through wine and the faults of drawing swords to contend for merit; in great cases one does not preserve one's life, in small cases one barely escapes.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the drunkard's insolence and the sword drawn for credit—some lose their lives, others barely escape.

sentences.zh: 耿豪、王勇不其然乎！

translations.literal: Were not Geng Hao and Wang Yong just such cases!
translations.idiomatic: Were Geng Hao and Wang Yong not exactly such cases!

sentences.zh: 李延孫、韋祐、陳欣、魏玄等以勇略之姿，受扞城之委。

translations.literal: Li Yansun, Wei You, Chen Xin, Wei Xuan, and the like with a brave and strategic bearing received the charge of defending cities.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yansun, Wei You, Chen Xin, Wei Xuan, and others—bold strategists entrusted with city defense—

sentences.zh: 灌瓜贈藥，雖有愧於昔賢；

translations.literal: Sending melons and bestowing medicine—though they fell short of the ancients;
translations.idiomatic: sent melons and medicine, falling short of ancient exemplars;

sentences.zh: 禦侮折沖，足方駕於前烈。

translations.literal: repelling insult and breaking the enemy's momentum—they fully matched former worthies.
translations.idiomatic: yet in repelling foes they matched the heroes of old.

sentences.zh: 用能觀兵伊、洛，保據崤、函，齊人阻西路之謀，周朝緩東貢之慮，皆其力也。

translations.literal: Thus they could review troops at Yi and Luo, hold fast to Xiao and Han, block Qi plans on the western road and ease Zhou worries over eastern tribute—all by their strength.
translations.idiomatic: They held Yi and Luo, guarded Xiao and Han, blocked Qi in the west and eased Zhou's eastern tribute worries—all by their own strength.

sentences.zh: 泉長自山谷，素無月旦之譽，而臨難慷慨，無失人臣之節，豈非蹈仁義之徒歟！

translations.literal: Quan Xian from the mountain valleys had never had a reputation for monthly judgment, yet facing peril he was generous and did not fail the integrity of a minister—is he not one who treads the path of benevolence and righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: Quan Xian, raised in the hills without renown for fine judgment, yet faced peril with steadfast loyalty—is he not a man of benevolence and righteousness!

sentences.zh: 元禮、仲遵，聿遵其志，卒成功業，庶乎克負荷矣。

translations.literal: Yuanli and Zhongzun followed his will and at last achieved success—perhaps they indeed bore the burden well.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli and Zhongzun kept his charge and finished the work—perhaps they truly bore the burden.

sentences.zh: 李遷哲、楊乾運、席固之徒，屬方隅擾攘，咸知委質，遂享爵位，以保終始。

translations.literal: Li Qianzhe, Yang Ganyun, Xi Gu, and their kind—in a disturbed corner all knew to submit and thus enjoyed rank and preserved their ends.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qianzhe, Yang Ganyun, Xi Gu, and the like, in troubled borderlands all knew when to submit and kept rank and life to the end.

sentences.zh: 觀遷哲之對周文，有尚義之氣。

translations.literal: Consider Qianzhe's reply to Zhou Wen—there was a spirit that honors righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe's answer to Zhou Wen showed a spirit that honors righteousness.

sentences.zh: 乾運受任武陵，乖事人之道。

translations.literal: Ganyun received appointment from Prince of Wuling and failed the way of serving one's lord.
translations.idiomatic: Ganyun's service under Prince of Wuling betrayed the way of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 若乃校其優劣，固不可同年而語。

translations.literal: If one compares their merits and faults they indeed cannot be spoken of in the same year.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against each other, they cannot be ranked alike.

sentences.zh: 陽雄任兼文武，聲著土內，抑亦志能之士也。

translations.literal: Yang Xiong's post combined civil and military roles and his fame resounded within the realm; he too was a man of will and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong held civil and military posts with fame throughout the land—he too was a man of talent and resolve.

sentences.zh: 舊史有代人宇文盛，字保興，以武毅顯，盛弟丘，字胡奴，盛子述，位柱國，並有傳。

translations.literal: The old histories have a man of the Dai clan Yuwen Sheng, style name Baoxing, who showed martial sternness; Sheng's younger brother Qiu, style name Hunu, Sheng's son Shu—all held the rank of Pillar of State—and all have biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Older histories record Yuwen Sheng of Dai, style Baoxing, famed for martial sternness; his brother Qiu, style Hunu, and son Shu, all Pillar of State, also had biographies.

sentences.zh: 然事無足可紀。

translations.literal: Yet their deeds were not worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their deeds were scarcely worth recording.

sentences.zh: 盛見子述傳首，丘略之云。

translations.literal: Sheng appears at the head of his son Shu's biography; Qiu is passed over briefly.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng appears only at the head of Shu's biography; Qiu is treated briefly.
